    Solver¶

    The solver layer holds the numerics: the Engine (configuration and solve), the FieldResult (potentials, currents, impedances, metadata) and the multi-port functions solve_mutual_matrix / solve_mutual_field. The backends themselves are registered in the backend registry; their theory is on the engine pages.

    Mathematical and physical context¶

    Every backend solves the same problem — the quasi-static potential of the electrodes in layered soil, coupled to the conductor network — for each frequency of Engine.frequencies. The electrodes are cut into \(N\) segments (length at most segment_length) carrying leakage currents \(I_k\); the potential of segment \(i\) is

    \[ \varphi_i = \sum_{k=1}^{N} G_{ik}\, I_k , \]

    with \(G_{ik}\) the potential at segment \(i\) per unit current on segment \(k\) (the Green's function of the layered half-space integrated over the segments). The galvanic clusters are equipotential, the conductor branches add Kirchhoff's laws, and the source currents are the right-hand side of the augmented system. The backends differ in how they evaluate \(G\) and which current ansatz they use:

    Backend Green's function Current ansatz
    image free space + surface image, closed form uniform current per unit length on each straight wire of an electrode (one unknown per wire line of a grid, arm of a star, straight run of a polyline, and soil layer; user decision Q30); exact line-source kernel by default
    image_2layer Tagg/Sunde image series, closed form; layered Sommerfeld correction for wires through the interface as image
    mom the same closed-form kernels point matching: one unknown current per segment, midpoint point sources
    mom_sommerfeld numerical Sommerfeld quadrature of the layered Green's function, any number of layers as mom
    fem (experimental) none: conforming finite elements of the soil, axisymmetric for coaxial rods and rings, three-dimensional otherwise (fem3d extra) volume solution (axisymmetric: the electrodes as solid bodies; 3-D: smoothed line sources)

    The uniform-current ansatz gives accurate impedances at low cost; near grids, stars, strip ends and bonded multi-electrode clusters its surface potentials are impedance-grade, not field-grade (see Known limitations).

    Engine(backend="image"), the default, forwards a TwoLayerSoil to image_2layer and a MultiLayerSoil with at most two distinct layers to the image dispatcher; three or more layers need mom_sommerfeld. FieldResult.metadata["effective_backend"] and ["kernel"] record what ran.

    Engine settings¶

    Field Default Meaning
    backend "image" registered backend name (see registry)
    frequencies [50.0] Hz; the given order is kept (a non-monotonic list warns with EngineFrequencyOrderWarning, with_frequencies(..., preserve_order=True) silences it)
    segment_length 0.5 maximum segment length in m
    kernel None None: the backend's preferred kernel ("line" for the image family); "line" or "point" explicitly; "point" reproduces the numbers of releases up to 0.15.0
    earth_inductive_model "sommerfeld" earth return of inductive conductors: "sommerfeld", "carson_series", "perfect_mirror" (see Coupling)
    sommerfeld_assembly "tabulated" assembly of the Sommerfeld correction of inductive conductors: "tabulated" (one table of the spectral integral per pair of depth groups and frequency; default since 2026.11) or "exact" (one quadrature per segment pair, the default up to 0.15.0)
    max_segments None resource limit of this engine: the largest number of leakage segments and of nodal unknowns it solves, ResourceLimitError above it before anything is allocated; None takes groundfield.diagnostics.HARD_LIMIT (20 000); recorded in metadata["max_segments"]
    warn_segments None size of the soft notice of this engine, counted like max_segments: at or above it the solve warns that it may take minutes (an info finding of diagnose); None takes groundfield.diagnostics.SOFT_LIMIT (5 000); not checked against max_segments (a notice above the hard limit never appears)
    image_max_terms, image_series_tol 300, 10⁻⁶ cap and stop tolerance of the Tagg/Sunde series (tail bound \(\lvert K\rvert^{n+1}/(1-\lvert K\rvert)\))
    image_far_field "quadrupole" form of the far images of the line kernel in two-layer soil (Tagg/Sunde images and images of the cross-layer correction): "quadrupole" (point value plus the quadrupole term of the segment average) or "point" (point sources beyond the near-pair reach: the dense far term is left out, the near image pairs stay Galerkin integrals on both paths, audit W3R2A-01; faster; networks move by 3 · 10⁻⁶ … 4.3 · 10⁻⁴, not the result before wave 3 of the 2026.11 work); any other value raises ValueError; recorded in metadata["series"], used by FieldResult.potential and solve_mutual_*; no effect with kernel="point" or in homogeneous soil (the author's decision of 2026-11-15)
    options {} backend-specific settings, e.g. {"mom_sommerfeld": {"epsrel": 1e-9}} (see the backend pages for the options of each backend)

    tolerance and max_iterations have no effect and are deprecated (see Deprecations).

    Example¶

    import groundfield as gf

world = gf.create_world(soil=gf.TwoLayerSoil(rho_1=100.0, rho_2=300.0, h_1=2.0))
gf.create_electrode(world, "rod", name="a", position=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), length=3.0)
gf.create_electrode(world, "ring", name="b", center=(20.0, 0.0, 0.8), radius=2.0)
engine = gf.create_engine(frequencies=[50.0])

# Mutual grounding-impedance matrix of the two earths in one assembly:
# Z[i, j] = potential of cluster i per ampere leaking from cluster j.
Z = gf.solve_mutual_matrix(world, engine, anchors=["a", "b"])   # Ω

# The same entries from an ordinary solve with 1 A at "a":
gf.create_source(world, attached_to="a", magnitude=1.0)
result = engine.solve(world)
assert abs(Z[0, 0] - result.cluster_impedance("a")[0]) < 1e-9    # 51.40 Ω
assert abs(Z[1, 0] - result.electrode_potentials["b"][0]) < 1e-9  # 2.26 Ω
assert result.metadata["effective_backend"] == "image_2layer"

    solve_mutual_matrix returns the galerkin off-diagonal (the reaction of the leakage distributions: reciprocal, and the matrix that reproduces a solve of the clusters joined by branches) for every call since 2026.11. offdiag="probe" with probe_points samples the potential at one point per cluster instead, the definition up to 0.15.0; probe points passed without it are ignored with a ProbePointsIgnoredWarning.

    FieldResult.potential(points, frequency_index=0) evaluates the potential in V at arbitrary points of shape (M, 3) (homogeneous and two-layer soil), to_dataframe() returns the per-electrode table, to_dataframe("sources") the per-source table (impressed or solved current, the voltage and internal impedance of a voltage source, the input impedance), and metadata["provenance"] records the package and library versions, the engine configuration, a fingerprint of the world and the solve time stamp. Results are saved and loaded with save_result / load_result.

    API reference¶

    engine ¶

    Numerical computation core (Engine).

    An Engine bundles everything that is purely numerical: the chosen backend (image, MoM, FEM, ...), the frequency list, the discretisation and the backend settings. It is deliberately separated from the World, so that the same physical configuration can be run against different backends.

    Backends are registered in groundfield.solver.registry, which records for each name the solve function, the declared capabilities (soil layer counts, conductor models, concrete shells, two-terminal sources, source kernels) and the backend-specific options model. The built-in backends fall into three families:

    Closed-form / image-charge. image is the homogeneous-soil image-charge sum (closed form, uniform current per unit length, cheapest backend). image_2layer implements the Tagg / Sunde geometric series for two-layer soil with convergence \(|K|^n\). Both use the exact line-source kernel by default (Engine.kernel). image_nlayer (deprecated name) routes a layered soil with one or two distinct layers to image / image_2layer and rejects three or more; cim is a deprecated name of the image auto-dispatch.

    Integral equation. mom solves for the segment currents by point matching (collocation) with the closed-form kernels above; mom_sommerfeld does the same with direct numerical Sommerfeld quadrature of the layered Green's function and is the only integral backend for \(n \ge 3\) layers. bem is a deprecated name of mom.

    Volume PDE. fem (experimental) solves the field in the soil by conforming finite elements: an axisymmetric model for rods on one axis and rings around it, a three-dimensional one for every other world (the optional fem3d extra), described in groundfield.solver.fem.

    Notes

    Engine.solve() performs an automatic dispatch when backend="image" is requested: the call is forwarded to "image_2layer" if the world holds a TwoLayerSoil, and to "image_nlayer" if it holds a MultiLayerSoil. Notebooks written for the homogeneous case therefore keep working when the soil is replaced by a layered one.

    Every result carries the metadata core CORE_METADATA_KEYS, filled here for all backends, next to the backend-specific keys.

    Backend module-attribute ¶

    Backend = Literal['image', 'image_2layer', 'image_nlayer', 'cim', 'mom', 'mom_sommerfeld', 'bem', 'fem']

    Names of the built-in backends, for type hints.

    The registry is the authority at runtime and also accepts registered third-party names (available_backends()). "cim", "bem" and "image_nlayer" are deprecated aliases of "image" and "mom".

    CORE_METADATA_KEYS module-attribute ¶

    CORE_METADATA_KEYS: tuple[str, ...] = ('backend', 'effective_backend', 'kernel', 'groundfield_version', 'frequencies', 'n_segments', 'soil_kind', 'earth_inductive_model', 'solve_time_s', 'series', 'max_segments', 'provenance')

    Metadata keys that Engine.solve() writes into every result.

    • backend: Backend name as requested (Engine.backend).
    • effective_backend: Registered backend that ran, after alias resolution and the auto-forwarding by soil model.
    • kernel: Source kernel used ("point" / "line"); fem reports the kernel of the point sources of its result (the engine's, default "line"), which the field evaluation uses.
    • groundfield_version: Version of the package that solved.
    • frequencies: Frequencies in Hz, in solve order.
    • n_segments: Number of current-carrying source segments (for fem the display segments that carry the point sources of its result).
    • soil_kind: kind of the soil model ("homogeneous", "two_layer", "multi_layer").
    • earth_inductive_model: Earth model of the inductive coupling.
    • solve_time_s: Wall time of the backend call in s.
    • series: Image-series controls of the engine, {"max_terms", "tol", "far_field"}, for the post-solve field evaluation.
    • max_segments: Problem-size limit the solve was checked against (Engine.max_segments, or groundfield.diagnostics.HARD_LIMIT when the engine leaves it at None); fem checks its display segments against it and limits its mesh by FemOptions.max_nodes / max_nodes_3d.
    • provenance: Versions, platform, engine configuration, world fingerprint and UTC timestamp (see groundfield.solver.result.solve_provenance()).

    DEFAULT_IMAGE_MAX_TERMS module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_IMAGE_MAX_TERMS = 300

    Default cap on the number of Tagg / Sunde image-series terms.

    One value for the engine, every layered backend and the post-solve field evaluation. The geometric tail bound |K|^(n+1)/(1-|K|) falls below the default tolerance after 277 terms for the AP1 corner soil rho_1 = 1000, rho_2 = 30 Ohm m (|K| = 0.9417), so the cap stays unused there.

    DEFAULT_IMAGE_SERIES_TOL module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_IMAGE_SERIES_TOL = 1e-06

    Default stop tolerance of the Tagg / Sunde image series.

    Summation ends when the geometric tail bound |K|^(n+1)/(1-|K|) falls below this value.

    DEFAULT_KERNEL module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_KERNEL = 'line'

    Kernel an engine requests when it leaves the choice to the backend.

    Applies to Engine.kernel = None, the default since 2026.11 (review pass 10, 10.28): the exact line-source kernel wherever a backend implements it (the image family), the backend's own kernel elsewhere.

    EarthInductiveModel module-attribute ¶

    EarthInductiveModel = Literal['perfect_mirror', 'carson_series', 'sommerfeld']

    Earth-return models of the inductive coupling.

    The values of Engine.earth_inductive_model:

    • "perfect_mirror": the earth as a perfect magnetic mirror (ADR-0004), a fast diagnostic baseline;
    • "carson_series": Carson's (1926) per-metre series correction for long parallel wires over homogeneous earth (ADR-0005);
    • "sommerfeld": the geometric Sommerfeld / Pollaczek integral for any geometry and any number of layers (ADR-0006), the engine's default.

    Engine ¶

    Bases: BaseModel

    Configuration of the numerical kernel.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    backend str

    Numerical method, a name registered in groundfield.solver.registry. Built in: image, image_2layer, image_nlayer, cim, mom, mom_sommerfeld, bem, fem. See the module docstring above for the family overview, and ADR-0002 for the selection heuristic. An unknown name raises with the closest registered one as suggestion.
    frequencies list[float]

    Frequency list in Hz. Default [50.0].
    segment_length float

    Maximum segment length used to discretise the geometry, in m.
    max_segments int | None

    Resource limit of this engine: the largest problem size it solves, counted as the number of leakage segments and as the number of unknowns of the dense nodal system (current owners, nodes and branches, every conductor sub-piece included). A world above it raises ResourceLimitError before anything of that size is allocated, in every segment backend and in solve_mutual_matrix() / solve_mutual_field. None (default) takes groundfield.diagnostics.HARD_LIMIT (20 000), read at solve time; a positive integer raises or lowers the limit for this engine only (user decision Q17 of 2026.11, finding 10.06). The dense reaction matrix of \(N\) segments takes \(8N^2\) bytes (3.0 GiB at 20 000), the nodal system of \(n\) unknowns \(16n^2\) bytes; expected_segments() predicts both. The limit is recorded in FieldResult.metadata ["max_segments"]; fem checks the display segments of its result against it and limits its volume mesh by FemOptions.max_nodes / max_nodes_3d.
    warn_segments int | None

    Size of the soft notice of this engine, counted like max_segments: at or above it every solve emits a UserWarning that the solve time may run from seconds to minutes ("budget: ..."), and diagnose() reports it as an info finding. None (default) takes groundfield.diagnostics.SOFT_LIMIT (5 000), read at solve time; a positive integer moves the notice for this engine only, for instance up to the size a workstation solves in seconds (user decision Q31 of 2026.11). It is not checked against max_segments: a notice above the hard limit never appears, because such a world is refused first. Kept by JSON round trips, with_frequencies() and model_copy(); the provenance block of a result records the request.
    tolerance, max_iterations

    Deprecated, no effect (no backend reads them). A non-default value warns; both fields will be removed no earlier than 2027.5.
    earth_inductive_model EarthInductiveModel

    How the earth contributes to the inductive coupling between distributed-conductor segments (only effective when at least one conductor sets inductance_model = "neumann"):

    • "perfect_mirror" (ADR-0004, the pre-0.13 default) — the earth is a perfect magnetic mirror. Cheap, frequency-independent inductance assembly, but its additive image is far from the f < 1 kHz physics of buried conductors (audit finding F5); kept as a fast diagnostic baseline.
    • "carson_series" (ADR-0005) — the earth has finite conductivity. Carson 1926's per-metre earth-return correction \(\Delta Z'_\text{Carson}(\omega)\) is added to the Neumann matrix built on Carson's own baseline, the anti-parallel image (since 2026.11; up to 0.15.0 it was added to the additive perfect-mirror matrix, which roughly doubled the reactance, review pass 10, 10.20). It is tiled per metre of axial overlap, and only inside its validity domain: near-parallel pairs (\(|\cos\varphi| > 0.99\)) of near-horizontal segments (inclination below 8.1°) on one side of the surface; two conductors overlapping on one axis get the correction of touching wires. A pair across the surface has no anti-parallel baseline and couples through the field transmitted into the soil (carson_mixed_mutual_correction()). Oblique pairs and every pair and self term of a segment inclined by more than 8.1° get the Sommerfeld correction of a homogeneous earth of the same conductivity; at that boundary the result steps by the error of the per-metre model (13 % for two 1 km leads 2 m apart at 1 kHz; audit rounds 2 and 3). Asymptotically correct for long parallel wires over homogeneous earth; an approximation for short wires and for layered soil (the top layer's conductivity is used).
    • "sommerfeld" (ADR-0006, Pollaczek kernel since the 2026-07-08 audit, WP-C1) — geometric integration of the σ-dependent vector-potential Green's function over the actual segment-pair geometry, dispatched by conductor side: buried pairs carry the in-soil attenuation \(e^{-\gamma R}\) (and with it the positive earth-return resistance \(\approx \omega\mu_0/8\) per metre in the long-wire limit), overhead pairs use the air-side reflection (Carson's geometry). The Neumann matrix carries no image: the correction holds the whole earth effect, so conductors in or crossing the surface plane are solved too (since 2026.11). Supports layered earth; see sommerfeld_assembly for the assembly (tabulated by default). Limits: \(\sigma \to 0\) → free space (no image); \(\sigma \to \infty\) → screened (buried) / anti-parallel PEC image (overhead). Validated against Pollaczek's analytic \(K_0\) mutual and Carson's line impedance (tests/test_earth_return_benchmark.py). The default since 0.13.0 — the rigorous choice whenever a quantitative Z(f) matters.
    image_max_terms, image_series_tol

    Controls of the Tagg / Sunde image-charge series (maximum number of terms; stop tolerance on the geometric tail bound \(|K|^{n+1}/(1-|K|)\), dimensionless). Common to every layered backend that evaluates the series (image_2layer, mom, the delegated two-layer path of mom_sommerfeld; the deprecated names run these) and to solve_mutual_*; recorded in FieldResult.metadata["series"], which FieldResult.potential() uses for the post-solve field evaluation. Defaults: DEFAULT_IMAGE_MAX_TERMS (300) and DEFAULT_IMAGE_SERIES_TOL (1e-6).
    image_far_field Literal['quadrupole', 'point']

    Form of the far images of the line kernel in two-layer soil — the Tagg/Sunde images (n >= 1) and the images of the cross-layer correction beyond the near-pair reach (the author's decision of 2026-11-15):

    • "quadrupole" (default) — the far form of direct pairs: the point value plus the quadrupole term of the segment average, tapered off between 60 and 120 segment lengths of vertical distance (wave 3 of the 2026.11 work, finding 10.28).
    • "point" — point sources: the dense far term is left out. The near image pairs (within 7.5 segment lengths, a segment's own images included) stay Galerkin integrals blended into the point form, on the series and the cross-layer path alike, and so do the continuous switch (user decision D2) and the transverse distance of near image pairs. It is therefore not the result before wave 3: within the upper layer it differs from it by up to 2.3e-4 (16 house grids in 1000 / 30 Ω·m with \(h_1\) = 1.5 m, the blend of D2). Up to audit W3R2A-01 the cross-layer path kept the line form of the interface image only, so a long segment below the interface saw its own images as point sources: a 75 m strip below a 0.5 m top layer read -1.0e-3 at a segment length of 2.5 m and -58 % at 37.5 m; it is now within 1.1e-5 of its exact value at every segment length (500 / 100 and 1000 / 30 Ω·m).

    Against the default, "point" moves networks by 3e-6 … 4.3e-4 (16 house grids 0.4 m above a 1000 / 10 Ω·m interface: 4.3e-4), a straight wire 0.5 m above the interface by 4e-4 and the surface potential above it by up to 0.8 %. With numba it takes 1.1 … 1.3 times the solve before wave 3 on house grids within the upper layer. On the cross-layer path it takes 0.49 … 0.94 of the default's time (0.25 … 0.54 without numba), because the Galerkin near image pairs stay: 1.5 … 2.4 times the solve before wave 3 below thin top layers, 4.3 … 4.5 times with long pieces there, and 0.91 times (0.90 without numba) on a 40-house network in 1000 / 30 Ω·m with \(h_1\) = 1.5 m, whose transformer rods reach below \(h_1\) (performance page). Any other value raises ValueError (audit W3R2A-02). No effect with kernel="point", in homogeneous soil or on backends without the line kernel. Read by the image family and solve_mutual_*, recorded in FieldResult.metadata["series"] ("far_field") and used by FieldResult.potential(); kept by JSON round trips, with_frequencies(), model_copy() and the provenance block. The name follows image_max_terms / image_series_tol, the other controls of how the image series is evaluated.
    options Mapping[str, SerializeAsAny[BackendOptions] | Mapping[str, Any]]

    Backend-specific settings, keyed by backend name and validated against the backend's options model: {"mom_sommerfeld": MomSommerfeldOptions(...)} (quadrature accuracy) and {"fem": FemOptions(...)} (mesh and truncation). Plain mappings are accepted and validated into the options models; unknown option names raise with a suggestion. Options for a backend other than the selected one (or one it forwards to) emit BackendOptionsWarning. Entries put into the mapping in place (engine.options["fem"] = {...}) bypass that validation; they are validated when they are read (backend_options(), solve()). The 0.15.0 flat fields sommerfeld_lambda_max_factor, sommerfeld_epsabs, sommerfeld_epsrel and sommerfeld_max_osc_panels are still accepted (constructor, JSON, attribute access and model_copy()) and mapped onto options["mom_sommerfeld"] with a DeprecationWarning (the constructor drops a value equal to the default silently, so engine JSON of 0.15.0 loads without warnings).
    sommerfeld_assembly Literal['exact', 'tabulated']

    Assembly of the Sommerfeld earth-return correction of inductive conductors (earth_inductive_model="sommerfeld"):

    • "tabulated" (default since 2026.11, user decision Q16) — one table of the spectral integral \(S(\rho)\) per pair of depth groups and frequency (cubic spline, 100 nodes), the outer quadrature of all segment pairs vectorised. Blocks of fewer than 64 sub-segment pairs and blocks whose \(\lambda\) grid cannot resolve their largest distance (conductors in the surface plane) keep the per-pair rule.
    • "exact" — every segment pair with its own quadrature and 24 interpolation nodes of \(S(\rho)\); the default up to 0.15.0.

    On a TN network of 8 houses with an inductive PEN (78 inductive branches, four frequencies) the tabulated solve took 1.0 s CPU instead of 16.6 s, and its input impedance is within 2e-10 of two independent refined references (per-pair rule with 200 nodes, tables of 400 nodes, both with a refined \(\lambda\) grid; they agree to 2e-10), the per-pair rule within 1.2e-8. Read by every backend that assembles the inductive branches through the shared pipeline (the image family, mom, mom_sommerfeld) and by solve_mutual_*; see build_sommerfeld_correction_matrices(), method. The Sommerfeld fallback of carson_series for oblique pairs is always tabulated.
    kernel Literal['point', 'line'] | None

    Green's-function kernel of the image family (image, image_2layer and image_nlayer for one or two layers), also used by FieldResult.potential() and solve_mutual_matrix() / solve_mutual_field:

    • None (default since 2026.11) — the backend's preferred kernel: "line" for the image family, the backend's own kernel ("point") for every other backend. FieldResult.metadata["kernel"] records the kernel that ran.
    • "line" — every segment is a uniform line current (Galerkin form of the exact line-source potential, see groundfield.solver._line_kernel). In homogeneous soil it is exact for straight wires at any segment length. In two-layer soil the Tagg/Sunde images and the images of the cross-layer correction get the same treatment: near image pairs exact (with the transverse distance of the wire from the image, audit W3A-02), blended into the far form between six and 7.5 segment lengths, far images with the quadrupole term (image_far_field). A straight 10 m strip is within 3.6e-6 of its uniform-current resistance for ds = 0.125–2 m, not monotonically (point kernel: up to 22 %), a ring 1 cm above a 1000 / 30 Ω·m interface within 0.004 % of its exact thin-ring value, and a rod through the layer interface within 1.4e-6 of its exact two-owner value. Cost: a solve of 16 house grids (N = 1920 segments) takes 3.8 times as long as with "point" in homogeneous soil and 1.6 times in two-layer soil (\(h_1\) = 5 m) when numba is installed (it is used automatically), 5.8 and 1.4 times without it; the extra time grows with \(N^2\). The far images of a high contrast cost more: a 40-house network in 1000 / 30 Ω·m with \(h_1\) = 1.5 m takes 1.8 times the solve before wave 3 of the 2026.11 work with numba, 3.6 times without (image_far_field="point": 0.8 times).
    • "point" — each segment's current sits at its midpoint; reproduces the results of releases up to 0.15.0. Its row sums carry an error of about \(-0.23/L\), so the grounding resistance converges to a value 0.9–1.9 % below the exact uniform-current solution (review pass 10, 10.28).

    An explicit "line" on a backend without the line kernel raises BackendCapabilityError. The request is carried in the value: an engine rebuilt from its JSON, from with_frequencies or from a result's provenance block runs exactly like the original.
    Notes

    Every field is validated on construction, on assignment (engine.frequencies = [] raises) and in model_copy() (unlike pydantic's default model_copy, which stores update unchecked). Lists mutated in place are checked when the engine solves.

    Examples:

    >>> eng = Engine(backend="mom_sommerfeld", options={"mom_sommerfeld": {"epsabs": 1e-8}})
>>> eng.backend_options().epsabs
1e-08

    def backend_options(self, name: str | None = None) -> BackendOptions | None:
    """Options a backend runs with: the stored entry or the defaults.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name
        Backend name or alias. Default: :attr:`backend`.

    Returns
    -------
    BackendOptions or None
        The validated options model of the backend, or ``None`` for
        a backend without backend-specific options.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If an entry put into :attr:`options` in place does not
        validate (unknown backend or option name, wrong value).
    """
    key = _registry.options_key(self.backend if name is None else name)
    model = _registry.get_backend(key).options_model
    if model is None:
        return None
    stored = self._checked_options().get(key)
    return stored if stored is not None else model()

    def model_copy(
    self, *, update: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None, deep: bool = False
) -> Self:
    """Copy of the engine with ``update`` validated like the constructor.

    pydantic's ``model_copy`` stores ``update`` without validation; a
    deprecated flat name such as ``sommerfeld_epsrel`` was then
    shadowed by its property and silently ignored (audit A1-02), and
    an empty frequency list or a raw option mapping went through
    (A1-04).

    Parameters
    ----------
    update
        Field values to change. Validated together with the unchanged
        fields; the deprecated flat ``sommerfeld_*`` names are mapped
        onto ``options["mom_sommerfeld"]`` with a
        :class:`DeprecationWarning`.
    deep
        Deep copy instead of a shallow one.

    Returns
    -------
    Engine
        The copy (the receiver is not changed).

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a key of ``update`` is not a field (with a suggestion), a
        value does not validate, or a flat name contradicts
        ``update["options"]``.

    Notes
    -----
    Only warnings that the update introduces are emitted; those of
    the unchanged fields (e.g. a non-monotonic frequency list) were
    emitted when the engine was built.
    """
    if not update:
        return super().model_copy(deep=deep)
    fields = type(self).model_fields
    unknown = [
        k for k in update if k not in fields and k not in _LEGACY_SOMMERFELD_FIELDS
    ]
    if unknown:
        key = str(unknown[0])
        raise ValueError(
            f"Engine.model_copy: {key!r} is not a field."
            f"{did_you_mean(key, fields)} Fields: {', '.join(fields)}."
        )
    changes = dict(update)
    flat = {
        _LEGACY_SOMMERFELD_FIELDS[k]: changes.pop(k)
        for k in list(changes)
        if k in _LEGACY_SOMMERFELD_FIELDS
    }
    if flat:
        changes["options"] = self._options_with_flat(
            changes.get("options", self.options), flat, explicit="options" in update
        )
    # The unchanged fields as set on this engine (not the defaults), so
    # the copy keeps pydantic's ``model_fields_set`` semantics.
    base = {name: self.__dict__[name] for name in self.model_fields_set}
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as before:
        warnings.simplefilter("always")
        type(self).model_validate(base)
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as after:
        warnings.simplefilter("always")
        copy = type(self).model_validate({**base, **changes})
    seen = {(w.category, str(w.message)) for w in before}
    for w in after:
        if (w.category, str(w.message)) not in seen:
            warn_external(str(w.message), w.category)
    return super(Engine, copy).model_copy(deep=True) if deep else copy

    def solve(self, world: "World") -> FieldResult:
    """Run the simulation with the configured backend.

    Resolves :attr:`backend` in the registry, checks the backend's
    declared capabilities against ``world`` and runs it. When
    ``backend == "image"`` the backend is auto-forwarded to
    ``"image_2layer"`` for a
    :class:`~groundfield.soil.models.TwoLayerSoil` and to
    ``"image_nlayer"`` for a
    :class:`~groundfield.soil.models.MultiLayerSoil`, so notebooks
    written for the homogeneous case keep working when the soil
    model is replaced.

    The sources of ``world`` are snapshotted before the backend runs
    and restored afterwards onto the caller's objects, exactly as in
    :meth:`World.solve <groundfield.world.World.solve>`: solving
    never rewrites the input world, whichever entry point is used.

    Parameters
    ----------
    world : World
        The assembled world (soil, electrodes, conductors and at
        least one source) the backend should solve.

    Returns
    -------
    FieldResult
        Container with per-frequency potentials, currents, cluster
        impedances, the source snapshot and metadata: the core keys
        :data:`CORE_METADATA_KEYS` (including the provenance block)
        plus the backend-specific keys.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``world.soil`` is unset, ``world`` contains no electrodes,
        fails :meth:`World.check <groundfield.world.World.check>`
        (no current source, short-circuited source, zero or non-finite
        magnitude; the same for every backend and for
        :meth:`World.solve <groundfield.world.World.solve>`),
        :attr:`backend` is not registered, :attr:`frequencies` was
        emptied or given a non-finite or negative entry in place, or
        an entry put into :attr:`options` in place does not validate.
    KeyError
        If a source terminal or conductor end names no node of
        ``world`` (:meth:`World.check <groundfield.world.World.check>`).
    BackendCapabilityError
        If the backend cannot represent the world (soil layer count,
        concrete-shell electrodes, explicitly requested kernel). The
        message names the registered backends that can.
    ResourceLimitError
        If the predicted number of segments or of nodal unknowns
        exceeds :attr:`max_segments` (default
        :data:`groundfield.diagnostics.HARD_LIMIT`); raised before
        anything of that size is allocated (subclass of
        ``ValueError``).

    Warns
    -----
    BackendCapabilityWarning
        If the backend solves the world with a documented
        simplification (reduced conductor model, ignored
        ``return_to``).
    DeprecationWarning
        If :attr:`backend` is a deprecated alias.
    ExperimentalBackendWarning
        On the first solve with an experimental backend in a process.
    """
    if world.soil is None:
        raise ValueError("World has no soil model. Set one before calling solve().")
    if not world.electrodes:
        raise ValueError("World contains no electrodes.")
    # Assignments are validated; a list mutated in place is not (A1-04).
    _check_frequency_values(self.frequencies)
    # Central validation of references and excitation (10.66) for
    # every backend and entry point, a current source included: a world
    # without one solved to zeros in fem only and raised in every other
    # backend (audit round 2, A2S-05).
    world.check()

    resolved = _registry.resolve_backend(self.backend, world)
    _log.info(
        "Engine.solve: backend=%s (running %s), n_electrodes=%d, n_freq=%d",
        self.backend,
        resolved.spec.name,
        len(world.electrodes),
        len(self.frequencies),
    )
    with _guarded_sources(world):
        return self._run(world, resolved)

    def with_frequencies(
    self,
    *frequencies: float,
    preserve_order: bool = False,
) -> "Engine":
    """Return a copy of this engine with a new ``frequencies`` list.

    Parameters
    ----------
    *frequencies
        One or more frequencies in Hz. Variadic to make the
        common case readable: ``engine.with_frequencies(50, 5000)``.
    preserve_order
        If ``True``, the frequencies are stored verbatim and no
        non-monotonic warning is raised even for a decreasing or
        duplicate-bearing list. This is the explicit opt-in for
        sweeps that require a specific iteration order. If ``False``
        (default) the standard :func:`_validate_frequencies` checks
        run.

    Returns
    -------
    Engine
        A new :class:`Engine` instance — the receiver is **not**
        mutated.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> eng = Engine(backend="image").with_frequencies(50, 5000,
    ...                                                preserve_order=True)
    >>> eng.frequencies
    [50.0, 5000.0]
    """
    freqs = [float(f) for f in frequencies]
    # The scalar contract holds for *both* paths. Checking it here
    # as well as in the validator keeps the error attributable to
    # ``with_frequencies()`` rather than to a nested model rebuild.
    _check_frequency_values(freqs)
    data = self.model_dump()
    data["frequencies"] = freqs
    if preserve_order:
        # Re-validate the rest, but suppress the field validator's
        # monotone warning — a deliberately ordered sweep is the
        # documented opt-in.
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", EngineFrequencyOrderWarning)
            return self.__class__.model_validate(data)
    # Default path: run the full field validation, including the
    # monotone-order warning. ``model_copy(update=...)`` would skip
    # every validator (pydantic v2 semantics), which is the
    # pre-0.14.1 defect. Re-emit any warning at the caller's frame
    # so the notebook line that built the engine is the one shown.
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
        warnings.simplefilter("always")
        engine = self.__class__.model_validate(data)
    for entry in caught:
        warnings.warn(entry.message, entry.category, stacklevel=2)
    return engine

    EngineFrequencyOrderWarning ¶

    Bases: UserWarning

    Engine.frequencies is not strictly monotonically increasing.

    A dedicated category for the monotonic-order warning emitted by Engine._validate_frequencies(). Using a dedicated class lets notebook authors silence the diagnostic with a stable warnings.simplefilter("once", EngineFrequencyOrderWarning) — the default UserWarning filter deduplicates by message text, and because the message embeds the offending list literal, every distinct non-monotonic list triggers a fresh warning even when the underlying convention is the same.

    result ¶

    Result object of a simulation run.

    A FieldResult is the unified return value of Engine.solve() and World.solve(). It contains:

    • electrode_potentials / electrode_currents — node values per frequency, used to derive input and transfer impedances.
    • point_sources — the discretised current distribution. The post-processing layer can use these to evaluate the potential at arbitrary field points (contour plots, profiles, touch and step voltages).
    • soil_resistivity and soil — provide the parameters needed to evaluate the appropriate Green's function (homogeneous or 2-layer) inside potential().
    • sources — the source snapshot of the solve, read by FieldResult.input_impedance(): the impressed current of every current source; the impressed voltage and the solved current of every voltage source.
    • metadata — the core keys every backend reports (see groundfield.solver.engine.CORE_METADATA_KEYS), including the provenance block, plus backend-specific keys.
    Serialisation

    model_dump_json / model_validate_json round-trip a result losslessly and produce standard JSON (no NaN / Infinity tokens). Values that JSON cannot express in metadata are written as single-key tagged objects and restored on validation:

    • {"$float": "inf" | "-inf" | "nan"} — non-finite float;
    • {"$complex": [re, im]} — complex number;
    • {"$tuple": [...]} — tuple;
    • {"$dict": [[key, value], ...]} — mapping with non-string keys (e.g. penetration_depth keyed by frequency) or with a key that looks like a tag;
    • {"$ndarray": {"dtype": ..., "shape": [...], "data": [...]}} — numpy array (bool, integer, float, complex or string dtype).

    numpy scalars are stored as the equal Python scalar. The tag names are reserved: a metadata value that is a single-key mapping with one of the keys above is decoded on validation. The versioned file format around this JSON is groundfield.io.save_result() / groundfield.io.load_result().

    The decoder reads only what the encoder writes, so a result file from an untrusted source cannot allocate more memory than a small multiple of its own size: $ndarray dtypes are limited to bool, integer, float16 … float64, complex64 / complex128 and unicode strings (no object, datetime, void, structured or sub-array dtypes); the shape must match the number of items before anything is allocated; every item must be a scalar of the dtype's kind; a string array may take at most 64 bytes per character of its items (plus 4 KiB); and metadata may nest at most MAX_METADATA_DEPTH levels. A tag that breaks these rules raises ValueError naming the metadata key (a pydantic.ValidationError when it is read through validation). The encoder applies the same limits, so every file it writes loads.

    MAX_METADATA_DEPTH module-attribute ¶

    MAX_METADATA_DEPTH = 100

    Deepest nesting of containers the metadata codec writes and reads.

    Containers are lists, mappings, tuples and tagged objects.

    FieldResult ¶

    Bases: BaseModel

    Result of a field computation.

    cluster_impedance ¶

    cluster_impedance(electrode_name: str) -> list[complex]

    Grounding impedance of the galvanic cluster containing an electrode.

    Definition: \(Z_{\text{cluster}}(f) = \varphi_{\text{cluster}}/\sum_{e \in c} I_e\). For a stand-alone electrode this is identical to grounding_impedance(). For connected electrodes it corresponds to the parallel combination of the individual grounding admittances.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    electrode_name str

    Name of any electrode in the target cluster. The cluster members are looked up in clusters; if the electrode does not appear there it is treated as a stand-alone cluster [electrode_name].

    		 required

    Returns:

    Type Description
    list[complex]

    Complex cluster impedance per frequency in ohms, one entry per entry in frequencies. Frequencies for which the summed cluster current is exactly zero return nan.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    KeyError

    If the resolved cluster is empty, or if none of its members carries potential and current data.
    Notes

    The cluster potential is the length-weighted (Galerkin) average over all members,

    \[ \varphi_c \;=\; \frac{\sum_{e \in c} L_e\, \varphi_e} {\sum_{e \in c} L_e}, \qquad L_e = \sum_{k \in e} L_k , \]

    with the per-electrode lengths taken from point_sources. Since every member potential \(\varphi_e\) is itself the length-weighted average over that electrode's segments, \(\varphi_c\) is exactly the length-weighted average over the whole cluster surface — the quantity the augmented system constrains to one value (see solver/image.py, block 1 of the multi-port system).

    Up to 0.14.1 this method read members[0], i.e. the alphabetically first member name. Because the reported member potentials were unweighted segment means they did not agree with each other, so renaming an electrode changed the reported cluster impedance of an unchanged geometry (19.4393 Ω → 19.2314 Ω in the audit case, 2026-07-28, F11). With the weighted reduction the members agree to round-off for the image family and the result is invariant under renaming for every backend.

    Numerator and denominator run over different member sets, deliberately:

    • \(\varphi_c\) averages over members that carry both potential and current data — a member with no potential cannot contribute a term to the average.
    • \(\sum_e I_e\) sums over every member that carries current data, whether or not its potential was stored, because its injected current is part of the cluster total regardless.

    Every backend in this package populates both mappings for every member, so the two sets coincide in practice. They differ only for hand-built FieldResult instances, where restricting the current sum to the potential-carrying members would silently under-count the cluster current (audit 2026-07-29).

    def cluster_impedance(self, electrode_name: str) -> list[complex]:
    """Grounding impedance of the galvanic cluster containing an electrode.

    Definition: $Z_{\\text{cluster}}(f) =
    \\varphi_{\\text{cluster}}/\\sum_{e \\in c} I_e$. For a
    stand-alone electrode this is identical to
    :meth:`grounding_impedance`. For connected electrodes it
    corresponds to the parallel combination of the individual
    grounding admittances.

    Parameters
    ----------
    electrode_name : str
        Name of any electrode in the target cluster. The cluster
        members are looked up in :attr:`clusters`; if the
        electrode does not appear there it is treated as a
        stand-alone cluster ``[electrode_name]``.

    Returns
    -------
    list[complex]
        Complex cluster impedance per frequency in ohms, one entry
        per entry in :attr:`frequencies`. Frequencies for which
        the summed cluster current is exactly zero return ``nan``.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If the resolved cluster is empty, or if none of its members
        carries potential *and* current data.

    Notes
    -----
    The cluster potential is the **length-weighted (Galerkin)
    average** over all members,

    .. math::
        \\varphi_c \\;=\\;
        \\frac{\\sum_{e \\in c} L_e\\, \\varphi_e}
              {\\sum_{e \\in c} L_e},
        \\qquad
        L_e = \\sum_{k \\in e} L_k ,

    with the per-electrode lengths taken from
    :attr:`point_sources`. Since every member potential
    :math:`\\varphi_e` is itself the length-weighted average over
    that electrode's segments, :math:`\\varphi_c` is exactly the
    length-weighted average over the whole cluster surface — the
    quantity the augmented system constrains to one value (see
    ``solver/image.py``, block 1 of the multi-port system).

    Up to 0.14.1 this method read ``members[0]``, i.e. the
    *alphabetically first* member name. Because the reported
    member potentials were unweighted segment means they did not
    agree with each other, so renaming an electrode changed the
    reported cluster impedance of an unchanged geometry (19.4393 Ω
    → 19.2314 Ω in the audit case, 2026-07-28, F11). With the
    weighted reduction the members agree to round-off for the
    image family and the result is invariant under renaming for
    every backend.

    Numerator and denominator run over **different** member sets,
    deliberately:

    * :math:`\\varphi_c` averages over members that carry *both*
      potential and current data — a member with no potential
      cannot contribute a term to the average.
    * :math:`\\sum_e I_e` sums over every member that carries
      current data, whether or not its potential was stored,
      because its injected current is part of the cluster total
      regardless.

    Every backend in this package populates both mappings for
    every member, so the two sets coincide in practice. They
    differ only for hand-built :class:`FieldResult` instances,
    where restricting the current sum to the potential-carrying
    members would silently under-count the cluster current
    (audit 2026-07-29).
    """
    members, u = self._cluster_potential(electrode_name)
    n_freq = len(u)
    # The *denominator* runs over every member that has current
    # data, not over ``usable``: a member without potential data
    # cannot contribute to the weighted average, but its injected
    # current is still part of the cluster's total. Restricting the
    # sum to ``usable`` (0.15.0 development state) silently dropped
    # it and returned a too-large impedance instead of the
    # ``KeyError`` v0.14.1 raised — e.g. potentials {"a"} with
    # currents {"a": 1 A, "b": 1 A} and cluster ["a", "b"] gave
    # 10 V / 1 A = 10 Ω where 10 V / 2 A = 5 Ω is meant
    # (audit 2026-07-29). Not reachable through any shipped
    # backend, but ``FieldResult`` is public and user-constructible.
    current_members = [
        m
        for m in members
        if m in self.electrode_currents
        and len(self.electrode_currents[m]) >= n_freq
    ]
    i_sum = [
        sum(self.electrode_currents[m][k] for m in current_members)
        for k in range(n_freq)
    ]
    return [
        (uk / ik) if ik != 0 else complex("nan")
        for uk, ik in zip(u, i_sum, strict=False)
    ]

    def grounding_impedance(self, electrode_name: str) -> list[complex]:
    """Input impedance $Z(f) = U/I$ of an electrode.

    Parameters
    ----------
    electrode_name : str
        Name of the electrode whose input impedance is requested.
        Must be present in both :attr:`electrode_potentials` and
        :attr:`electrode_currents`.

    Returns
    -------
    list[complex]
        Complex impedance per frequency in ohms, one entry per
        entry in :attr:`frequencies`. Frequencies for which the
        electrode current is exactly zero return ``nan``.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If ``electrode_name`` is unknown to the result.

    Notes
    -----
    For galvanically connected electrodes (cluster with more than
    one member) this quantity is the cluster potential divided by
    the electrode's share of the total current. The physically
    meaningful quantity is the **cluster impedance** (see
    :meth:`cluster_impedance`).
    """
    if electrode_name not in self.electrode_potentials:
        raise KeyError(f"No potential data for '{electrode_name}'.")
    if electrode_name not in self.electrode_currents:
        raise KeyError(f"No current data for '{electrode_name}'.")
    u = self.electrode_potentials[electrode_name]
    i = self.electrode_currents[electrode_name]
    return [
        (uk / ik) if ik != 0 else complex("nan")
        for uk, ik in zip(u, i, strict=False)
    ]

    input_impedance ¶

    input_impedance(source: str | None = None) -> list[complex]

    Driving-point impedance seen by a source.

    Definition:

    \[ Z_\text{in}(f) \;=\; \frac{\varphi_a(f) - \varphi_r(f)}{I_s(f)}, \]

    with \(\varphi_a\) the potential of the galvanic cluster the source feeds (attached_to), \(\varphi_r\) the potential of the return cluster (return_to; zero for a return through remote earth) and \(I_s\) the source current. Cluster potentials are the length-weighted averages used by cluster_impedance().

    • Current source: \(I_s\) is the impressed current.
    • Voltage source (since 2026.11): the solve fixes \(\varphi_a - \varphi_r = U - Z_q I_s\), so \(Z_\text{in} = U / I_s - Z_q\) with the impressed voltage \(U\), the solved source current \(I_s\) and the internal impedance \(Z_q = R + j\omega L\) of the source (SourceRecord.voltage, SourceRecord.current, SourceRecord.internal_impedance()). It is the impedance the source sees at its terminals, without its own \(Z_q\) (the current is \(U / (Z_q + Z_\text{in})\)). For a world with this one source it equals the impedance a 1 A current source at the same terminals reports, to round-off; with several sources it is an apparent impedance (see Notes).

    This is the impedance a measurement instrument or a fault sees at the feeding point. It differs from cluster_impedance() (cluster potential over the cluster's own leakage current) as soon as part of the injected current leaves the cluster through conductors (PEN, cable shields, measurement leads): then the cluster impedance describes the local electrode only, the input impedance the whole connected system.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    source str | None

    Name of the source. May be omitted when the result carries exactly one source.

    		 None

    Returns:

    Type Description
    list[complex]

    Complex input impedance per frequency in ohms. Frequencies with zero source current return nan.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    If the result carries no source snapshot (hand-built results), no source, or several sources and source is omitted; if the record of a voltage source carries no solved current (a backend that does not report it).
    KeyError

    If source is unknown, or the feeding / return electrode has no potential data in this result.
    Notes

    With several simultaneous sources the potential difference includes the contribution of the other sources, so the ratio is an apparent impedance of the named source. Two 230 V sources on two 3 m rods 5 m apart (100 Ω·m, image) report 38.90 Ω each, against 35.99 Ω of the 1 A solve of one rod (+8.1 %).

    def input_impedance(self, source: str | None = None) -> list[complex]:
    """Driving-point impedance seen by a source.

    Definition:

    $$
    Z_\\text{in}(f) \\;=\\;
    \\frac{\\varphi_a(f) - \\varphi_r(f)}{I_s(f)},
    $$

    with $\\varphi_a$ the potential of the galvanic cluster the
    source feeds (``attached_to``), $\\varphi_r$ the potential of
    the return cluster (``return_to``; zero for a return through
    remote earth) and $I_s$ the source current. Cluster potentials
    are the length-weighted averages used by
    :meth:`cluster_impedance`.

    * **Current source:** $I_s$ is the impressed current.
    * **Voltage source** (since 2026.11): the solve fixes
      $\\varphi_a - \\varphi_r = U - Z_q I_s$, so
      $Z_\\text{in} = U / I_s - Z_q$ with the impressed voltage $U$,
      the solved source current $I_s$ and the internal impedance
      $Z_q = R + j\\omega L$ of the source
      (:attr:`SourceRecord.voltage`, :attr:`SourceRecord.current`,
      :meth:`SourceRecord.internal_impedance`). It is the impedance
      the source sees at its terminals, **without** its own $Z_q$
      (the current is $U / (Z_q + Z_\\text{in})$). For a world with
      this one source it equals the impedance a 1 A current source
      at the same terminals reports, to round-off; with several
      sources it is an apparent impedance (see *Notes*).

    This is the impedance a measurement instrument or a fault sees
    at the feeding point. It differs from :meth:`cluster_impedance`
    (cluster potential over the cluster's own *leakage* current)
    as soon as part of the injected current leaves the cluster
    through conductors (PEN, cable shields, measurement leads):
    then the cluster impedance describes the local electrode only,
    the input impedance the whole connected system.

    Parameters
    ----------
    source
        Name of the source. May be omitted when the result carries
        exactly one source.

    Returns
    -------
    list[complex]
        Complex input impedance per frequency in ohms. Frequencies
        with zero source current return ``nan``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the result carries no source snapshot (hand-built
        results), no source, or several sources and ``source`` is
        omitted; if the record of a voltage source carries no solved
        current (a backend that does not report it).
    KeyError
        If ``source`` is unknown, or the feeding / return electrode
        has no potential data in this result.

    Notes
    -----
    With several simultaneous sources the potential difference
    includes the contribution of the other sources, so the ratio is
    an *apparent* impedance of the named source. Two 230 V sources
    on two 3 m rods 5 m apart (100 Ω·m, ``image``) report 38.90 Ω
    each, against 35.99 Ω of the 1 A solve of one rod (+8.1 %).
    """
    if not self.sources:
        raise ValueError(
            "input_impedance needs the source snapshot of the solve; "
            "this result carries none (hand-built FieldResult?)."
        )
    candidates = [s for s in self.sources if s.kind in _SOURCE_KINDS]
    if source is None:
        if not candidates:
            raise ValueError("The result carries no current source.")
        if len(candidates) > 1:
            kinds = {s.kind for s in candidates}
            label = f"{kinds.pop()} sources" if len(kinds) == 1 else "sources"
            names = ", ".join(s.name for s in candidates)
            raise ValueError(
                f"The result carries several {label} ({names}); pass source=<name>."
            )
        record = candidates[0]
    else:
        by_name = {s.name: s for s in self.sources}
        if source not in by_name:
            known = ", ".join(sorted(by_name)) or "none"
            raise KeyError(f"Unknown source {source!r} (known: {known}).")
        record = by_name[source]
        if record.kind not in _SOURCE_KINDS:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Source {source!r} is a {record.kind!r} source; the input "
                "impedance is defined for current and voltage sources."
            )
    if record.kind == "voltage":
        n_freq = len(self.frequencies)
        if len(record.current) != n_freq or len(record.voltage) != n_freq:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Voltage source {record.name!r}: the result carries no "
                "solved source current (the backend did not report it), "
                f"or not one per frequency ({len(record.current)} currents, "
                f"{len(record.voltage)} voltages, {n_freq} frequencies)."
            )
        z_in = [
            u / i if i != 0 else complex("nan")
            for u, i in zip(record.voltage, record.current, strict=True)
        ]
        if record.internal_resistance_ohm or record.internal_inductance_h:
            # The impedance seen by the source, without its own Z_q.
            z_in = [
                z - record.internal_impedance(f)
                for z, f in zip(z_in, self.frequencies, strict=True)
            ]
        return z_in
    u_a = self._terminal_potential(record.name, "feeds", record.attached_to)
    if record.return_to is None:
        u_r = [0j] * len(u_a)
    else:
        u_r = self._terminal_potential(record.name, "returns to", record.return_to)
    return [
        (ua - ur) / ik if ik != 0 else complex("nan")
        for ua, ur, ik in zip(u_a, u_r, record.current, strict=False)
    ]

    potential ¶

    potential(points: ndarray, frequency_index: int = 0, min_distance: float = 0.001) -> np.ndarray

    Evaluate the potential at field points (image-charge sum).

    Picks the appropriate Green's-function kernel automatically:

    • homogeneous (HomogeneousSoil or no self.soil set but soil_resistivity available): classic image-charge sum \(1/r + 1/r_{\text{img}}\).
    • 2-layer (TwoLayerSoil, or MultiLayerSoil with exactly two layers): Tagg/Sunde series truncated with the controls of the solve, metadata["series"] (the engine's image_max_terms and image_series_tol; defaults 300 and 1e-6 for results without the record).
    • 1-layer (MultiLayerSoil with a single layer): degenerate case, dispatched to the homogeneous kernel.

    The dispatch reads the canonical layer stack of self.soil (adjacent layers of one resistivity merged, review pass 10, 10.48): TwoLayerSoil(rho, rho, h) and a MultiLayerSoil of one resistivity are evaluated like homogeneous soil, exactly as they are solved (before audit A3S-04 their sources below h took the point form of the two-layer kernel, +2.7 % next to a rod), and a MultiLayerSoil with at most two distinct layers like the two-layer soil.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    points ndarray

    Field points, array of shape (M, 3) in metres.

    		 required
    frequency_index int

    Index into frequencies. Default 0.

    		 0
    min_distance float

    Numerical cutoff for 1/r singularities, in metres.

    		 0.001

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    phi (ndarray, shape(M))

    Complex potential in V.

    Warns:

    Type Description
    SeriesTruncationWarning

    If the two-layer series reaches max_terms before its tail bound falls below tol.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    NotImplementedError

    If self.soil is a MultiLayerSoil with three or more distinct layers. The post-solve potential path does not yet carry an n-layer Green's-function kernel. The solve itself is still correct via the cim / mom_sommerfeld / bem backends — only the explicit potential() evaluation is unavailable for n ≥ 3. Cluster impedances, electrode currents and potentials stored in electrode_potentials / cluster_impedance remain accessible.
    Notes

    Prior to 0.2.0 a MultiLayerSoil with n ≥ 3 silently fell through to the homogeneous kernel, returning incorrect potentials, profiles, touch / step voltages and VTK exports. The error is now raised explicitly so the regime is visible rather than silent.

    Point sources at projected (UTM) coordinates, beyond 10 km from the origin, are evaluated in a local frame: points and sources are shifted by the rounded centre of the sources' bounding box (exact for nearby doubles) before the kernel runs (since 2026.11; see Units and conventions in the reference).

    def potential(
    self,
    points: np.ndarray,
    frequency_index: int = 0,
    min_distance: float = 1e-3,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Evaluate the potential at field points (image-charge sum).

    Picks the appropriate Green's-function kernel automatically:

    - **homogeneous** (:class:`HomogeneousSoil` or no ``self.soil``
      set but ``soil_resistivity`` available): classic image-charge
      sum $1/r + 1/r_{\\text{img}}$.
    - **2-layer** (:class:`TwoLayerSoil`, or :class:`MultiLayerSoil`
      with exactly two layers): Tagg/Sunde series truncated with the
      controls of the solve, ``metadata["series"]`` (the engine's
      ``image_max_terms`` and ``image_series_tol``; defaults 300 and
      ``1e-6`` for results without the record).
    - **1-layer** (:class:`MultiLayerSoil` with a single layer):
      degenerate case, dispatched to the homogeneous kernel.

    The dispatch reads the canonical layer stack of ``self.soil``
    (adjacent layers of one resistivity merged, review pass 10,
    10.48): ``TwoLayerSoil(rho, rho, h)`` and a ``MultiLayerSoil`` of
    one resistivity are evaluated like homogeneous soil, exactly as
    they are solved (before audit A3S-04 their sources below ``h``
    took the point form of the two-layer kernel, +2.7 % next to a
    rod), and a ``MultiLayerSoil`` with at most two distinct layers
    like the two-layer soil.

    Parameters
    ----------
    points
        Field points, array of shape ``(M, 3)`` in metres.
    frequency_index
        Index into :attr:`frequencies`. Default 0.
    min_distance
        Numerical cutoff for 1/r singularities, in metres.

    Returns
    -------
    phi : np.ndarray, shape (M,)
        Complex potential in V.

    Warns
    -----
    SeriesTruncationWarning
        If the two-layer series reaches ``max_terms`` before its tail
        bound falls below ``tol``.

    Raises
    ------
    NotImplementedError
        If ``self.soil`` is a :class:`MultiLayerSoil` with three or
        more distinct layers. The post-solve potential path does not yet
        carry an n-layer Green's-function kernel. The solve itself
        is still correct via the ``cim`` / ``mom_sommerfeld`` /
        ``bem`` backends — only the explicit
        :meth:`potential` evaluation is unavailable for n ≥ 3.
        Cluster impedances, electrode currents and potentials
        stored in :attr:`electrode_potentials` /
        :attr:`cluster_impedance` remain accessible.

    Notes
    -----
    Prior to 0.2.0 a :class:`MultiLayerSoil` with n ≥ 3 silently
    fell through to the homogeneous kernel, returning incorrect
    potentials, profiles, touch / step voltages and VTK exports.
    The error is now raised explicitly so the regime is visible
    rather than silent.

    Point sources at projected (UTM) coordinates, beyond 10 km from
    the origin, are evaluated in a local frame: points and sources are
    shifted by the rounded centre of the sources' bounding box (exact
    for nearby doubles) before the kernel runs (since 2026.11; see
    *Units and conventions* in the reference).
    """
    if not self.point_sources:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "FieldResult has no point_sources — the backend did not "
            "populate the post-processing data (stub?)."
        )

    pts = np.asarray(points, dtype=float)
    if pts.ndim == 1:
        pts = pts[None, :]
    if pts.shape[1] != 3:
        raise ValueError(f"points must have shape (M, 3), got {pts.shape}.")

    sources, all_currents = self._point_source_arrays()
    # Contiguous, as before the cache: the real/imaginary views then
    # have the stride the BLAS calls of v0.15.0 saw.
    currents = np.ascontiguousarray(all_currents[:, frequency_index])
    line = self._line_sources()
    # Sources at projected (UTM) coordinates: evaluate in a local frame
    # of the sources, exactly shifted (2026.11, see solver._frame); a
    # result within 10 km of the origin is evaluated as before.
    from groundfield.solver._frame import points_origin

    origin = points_origin(sources)
    if origin is not None:
        pts = pts - origin
        sources = sources - origin
        if line is not None:
            from groundfield.solver._line_kernel import LineSegments

            line = LineSegments(
                line.mid - origin, line.length, line.tangent, line.radius
            )

    # Dispatch to the kernel that matches the effective number of
    # soil layers: that of the canonical layer stack, the soil the
    # backends actually solve (review pass 10, 10.48). A
    # ``TwoLayerSoil(rho, rho, h)`` or a ``MultiLayerSoil`` of one
    # resistivity is homogeneous soil — its sources below h took the
    # point form of the two-layer spectral kernel here instead of the
    # line sources of the homogeneous result (+2.7 % next to a rod,
    # audit A3S-04); a ``MultiLayerSoil`` with one or two distinct
    # layers is cast on the fly. For n ≥ 3 there is no closed-form
    # image-charge series (Γ_1(λ) is no longer constant in λ — see
    # ``solver/image_nlayer.py``), so the call is rejected explicitly
    # rather than silently falling back to the homogeneous kernel.
    soil = self.soil
    if soil is not None and not isinstance(soil, HomogeneousSoil):
        from groundfield.solver._layered import canonical_soil

        soil = canonical_soil(soil)
    if isinstance(soil, TwoLayerSoil):
        return self._potential_two_layer(
            pts, sources, currents, soil, min_distance, line=line
        )
    if isinstance(soil, MultiLayerSoil):
        n = len(soil.layers)
        raise NotImplementedError(
            f"FieldResult.potential: MultiLayerSoil with n={n} ≥ 3 "
            "layers is not supported on the post-solve potential "
            "path. The solve itself is correct (use the "
            "'mom_sommerfeld' or 'fem' backend), but a closed-form "
            "n-layer Green's-function kernel is not yet wired into "
            "FieldResult.potential. Access cluster impedances and "
            "electrode potentials directly via "
            "result.electrode_potentials / result.cluster_impedance "
            "instead, or reduce the soil model to "
            "TwoLayerSoil / HomogeneousSoil for explicit field "
            "evaluation."
        )
    if isinstance(soil, HomogeneousSoil) and soil is not self.soil:
        # A layered declaration of one resistivity (see above).
        return self._potential_homogeneous(
            pts,
            sources,
            currents,
            min_distance,
            rho_override=float(soil.rho),
            line=line,
        )
    return self._potential_homogeneous(
        pts, sources, currents, min_distance, line=line
    )

    def to_dataframe(self, table: str = "electrodes") -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Tidy table of the result, one row per frequency and object.

    Parameters
    ----------
    table
        ``"electrodes"`` (default): one row per frequency and
        electrode with the columns

        * ``frequency_hz`` — frequency in Hz;
        * ``electrode`` — electrode name;
        * ``cluster`` — galvanic cluster, labelled by its
          alphabetically first member (see :attr:`clusters`);
        * ``potential_v`` — electrode potential in V (complex);
        * ``current_a`` — leakage current of the electrode into the
          soil in A (complex);
        * ``cluster_impedance_ohm`` — :meth:`cluster_impedance` of
          the electrode's cluster in Ω (complex), the cluster
          potential over the cluster's own leakage current.

        ``"sources"``: one row per frequency and recorded source
        with ``frequency_hz``, ``source``, ``kind``,
        ``attached_to``, ``return_to``, ``current_a`` (source
        current in A, complex: impressed, or solved for a voltage
        source), ``voltage_v`` (impressed voltage in V of a voltage
        source, complex; ``nan`` for a current source),
        ``internal_resistance_ohm`` and ``internal_inductance_h``
        (internal impedance of a voltage source in Ω and H, float;
        ``nan`` for a current source) and ``input_impedance_ohm``
        (:meth:`input_impedance` in Ω, complex), the impedance seen
        at the feeding point (without the internal impedance).

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        The table; rows ordered by frequency, then by electrode /
        source in result order. Values that the result does not
        carry (hand-built results) are ``nan``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``table`` is not ``"electrodes"`` or ``"sources"``.
    ImportError
        If pandas is not installed (it is imported on first use).

    Examples
    --------
    >>> df = result.to_dataframe()                       # doctest: +SKIP
    >>> df.pivot(index="frequency_hz", columns="electrode",
    ...          values="potential_v").abs()             # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    if table not in ("electrodes", "sources"):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown table {table!r}; choose 'electrodes' or 'sources'."
        )
    try:
        import pandas as pd
    except ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - pandas is a dependency
        raise ImportError(
            "FieldResult.to_dataframe needs pandas (pip install pandas)."
        ) from exc
    if table == "sources":
        return self._source_frame(pd)
    return self._electrode_frame(pd)

    PointSource ¶

    Bases: BaseModel

    A discretised current source (segment midpoint, length, direction).

    Filled by the backend; not instantiated directly by the user. With the point kernel the current sits at position; with the line kernel (FieldResult.metadata["kernel"] == "line") it is spread uniformly along the segment given by length and direction.

    SourceRecord ¶

    Bases: BaseModel

    Snapshot of one source as it was solved.

    Filled by Engine.solve() (and, for a world with voltage sources, by the backend); not instantiated directly by the user. FieldResult.input_impedance() reads it, so the result stays self-contained after the world has changed.

    For a current source current is the impressed current and voltage is empty. For a voltage source voltage is the impressed voltage \(U\) and current the source current \(I\) the solve returned — the current the source drives into attached_to (and takes back from return_to), the same sign convention as a current source; internal_resistance_ohm and internal_inductance_h are its internal impedance \(Z_q = R + j\omega L\) (0 for an ideal source and for current sources), so the terminal voltage is \(U - Z_q I\).

    A record pickled before 2026.11 lacks the two fields of the internal impedance and unpickles with 0 / 0, as its JSON loads (audit W2R2-01).

    internal_impedance ¶

    internal_impedance(frequency: float) -> complex

    Internal impedance \(Z_q = R + j\omega L\) in Ω at frequency (Hz).

    0j for a current source and an ideal voltage source.

    def internal_impedance(self, frequency: float) -> complex:
    """Internal impedance $Z_q = R + j\\omega L$ in Ω at ``frequency`` (Hz).

    ``0j`` for a current source and an ideal voltage source.
    """
    return _internal_impedance(
        self.internal_resistance_ohm,
        self.internal_inductance_h,
        2.0 * np.pi * float(frequency),
    )

    def solve_provenance(world: World, engine: Engine) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Provenance block of a solve (without the timestamp).

    :meth:`Engine.solve <groundfield.solver.engine.Engine.solve>` calls
    this before the backend runs and adds ``solved_at_utc`` when it
    returns; the block is stored as ``FieldResult.metadata["provenance"]``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    world
        The world as built by the caller.
    engine
        The engine configuration.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        ``groundfield_version``, ``python``, ``numpy``, ``scipy``,
        ``pydantic``, ``platform``, ``engine`` (the JSON dump of the
        engine) and ``world_fingerprint`` (see :func:`world_fingerprint`).
    """
    block: dict[str, Any] = dict(_environment())
    block["engine"] = engine.model_dump(mode="json")
    block["world_fingerprint"] = world_fingerprint(world)
    return block

    def world_fingerprint(world: World) -> str:
    """SHA-256 fingerprint of the canonical JSON of a world.

    The canonical form is ``json.dumps(world.model_dump(mode="json"),
    sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))``. Pydantic writes floats in
    their shortest round-trip form, so equal worlds give equal
    fingerprints, also after a JSON round trip of the world. The
    fingerprint depends on the world schema of the installed version:
    renamed or added model fields change it.

    Parameters
    ----------
    world
        The world to fingerprint.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        ``"sha256:"`` followed by 64 hexadecimal digits.
    """
    canonical = json.dumps(
        world.model_dump(mode="json"), sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")
    )
    return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

    mutual ¶

    Mutual grounding-impedance matrix and field matrix in one assembly.

    solve_mutual_matrix() computes the full nG × nG mutual grounding-impedance matrix Z_G of a set of grounding clusters ("gnodes"), solve_mutual_field() the potential at arbitrary points per unit excitation, each in one matrix assembly instead of one Engine.solve per excitation.

    Motivation

    The AP1 catalogue builds Z_G for every site and soil. The historic loop (one world per excitation, cluster_impedance on the diagonal, FieldResult.potential at a probe point off the diagonal) assembled the N × N segment reaction matrix nG times. Here:

    1. The segment reaction matrix is assembled once, directly (the kernel operators' matrix method; v0.15.0 applied the kernel to an N × N identity, one O(N³) product per image term — review pass 10, 10.59), including the ADR-0012 V2 concrete shell.
    2. The leakage distribution of every excitation is a solve of the same augmented nodal system as Engine.solve(), with one owner per straight wire of an electrode (a wire line of a grid, an arm of a star, an edge of a polyline; user decision Q30) and per soil layer for electrodes through the layer interface (10.15).
    3. The off-diagonal entries are either the reaction of the leakage columns (offdiag="galerkin", the default, no further kernel evaluation) or the probe-point potentials (offdiag="probe", one probe kernel for all columns).

    Discretisation, topology and the branch block come from the shared image-family pipeline (groundfield.solver._pipeline); only the image family is accepted (10.34).

    Consistency with Engine.solve

    The diagonal equals FieldResult.cluster_impedance() of a per-excitation solve with the same engine to round-off (10.26), probe off-diagonals equal FieldResult.potential() at the probe point, and the columns of solve_mutual_field() equal FieldResult.potential at the field points (tests/test_mutual_matrix.py, tests/test_mutual_field.py).

    OffDiagonal module-attribute ¶

    OffDiagonal = Literal['probe', 'galerkin']

    Off-diagonal definitions of solve_mutual_matrix() (10.34).

    "galerkin" (the default since 2026.11): the reaction of the leakage distributions, reciprocal; "probe": the potential at one probe point per cluster, the definition up to 0.15.0.

    ProbePointsIgnoredWarning ¶

    Bases: UserWarning

    solve_mutual_matrix was given probe points it does not use.

    Since the user decision Q15 of 2026.11 the off-diagonal of solve_mutual_matrix() is offdiag="galerkin" whatever the call. Up to 0.15.0 passing probe_points selected the potential at those points as the off-diagonal; such a call now returns the galerkin matrix, ignores the points and emits this warning. Pass offdiag="probe" to keep the 0.15.0 definition, or drop the probe points.

    solve_mutual_field ¶

    solve_mutual_field(world: 'World', engine: 'Engine', anchors: list[str], field_points: ndarray, *, frequency_index: int = 0, matrix_min_distance: float = 0.001, matrix_max_terms: int | None = None, matrix_tol: float | None = None) -> np.ndarray

    Galvanic Green-function matrix: potential at arbitrary field points per node.

    Returns R of shape (M, nG) with R[i, j] = potential at field_points[i] (x, y, depth) under unit current (1 A) injected into anchors[j] while all other clusters stay floating. This is the off-diagonal field evaluation of solve_mutual_matrix(), generalised to an arbitrary number of field points (decoupled from nG) and without the self/diagonal term — the building block for the frequency-dependent surface-potential distribution by superposition::

    phi(field_points, f) = R @ I_leak(f)

    with I_leak(f) = Y_G @ u(f) from the reduced network (Y_L(f) + Y_G) u = i. Uses the same one-shot assembly as solve_mutual_matrix() (reaction matrix and per-excitation leakage columns built once); only the field-point evaluation is generalised. The expensive 3D part is therefore frequency-independent and computed once, so a frequency sweep over I_leak(f) is cheap.

    world must already carry all nG grounding clusters (every anchor in anchors must be a real electrode in world) and the soil model. Any current source is ignored — the excitations are applied internally, one cluster at a time, exactly as the historic per-excitation loop did.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    world 'World'

    Assembled world holding all nG grounding clusters and the soil model. Sources, if any, are ignored.

    		 required
    engine 'Engine'

    Engine configuration. segment_length controls the discretisation; frequencies selects the solved frequency via frequency_index; image_max_terms / image_series_tol feed the 2-layer self-kernel (the reaction-matrix assembly), exactly as Engine.solve would.

    		 required
    anchors list[str]

    Length-nG list of electrode names, one per node. Anchor j receives the unit current of excitation j and fills column j of R.

    		 required
    field_points ndarray

    (M, 3) array of (x, y, depth) evaluation points, decoupled from nG: M may differ from nG and the points are arbitrary (surface or buried). Row i becomes row i of R.

    		 required
    frequency_index int

    Index into engine.frequencies. Default 0. Only relevant when distributed conductors make the assembled system frequency-dependent.

    		 0
    matrix_min_distance float

    Clamp distance in m and series controls of the field evaluation. None (default) for the series controls takes engine.image_max_terms / engine.image_series_tol, the controls FieldResult.potential() uses after a solve with the same engine (before 2026.11 they were hard-coded to 100 / 1e-6, review pass 10, 10.25).

    		 0.001

None (default) for the series controls takes engine.image_max_terms / engine.image_series_tol, the controls FieldResult.potential() uses after a solve with the same engine (before 2026.11 they were hard-coded to 100 / 1e-6, review pass 10, 10.25).
