    def solve_mutual_field(
    world: "World",
    engine: "Engine",
    anchors: list[str],
    field_points: np.ndarray,
    *,
    frequency_index: int = 0,
    matrix_min_distance: float = 1e-3,
    matrix_max_terms: int | None = None,
    matrix_tol: float | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Galvanic Green-function matrix: potential at arbitrary field points per node.

    Returns ``R`` of shape ``(M, nG)`` with ``R[i, j]`` = potential at
    ``field_points[i]`` (``x, y, depth``) under unit current (1 A) injected
    into ``anchors[j]`` while all other clusters stay floating. This is the
    off-diagonal field evaluation of :func:`solve_mutual_matrix`, generalised
    to an **arbitrary** number of field points (decoupled from ``nG``) and
    without the self/diagonal term — the building block for the
    frequency-dependent surface-potential distribution by superposition::

        phi(field_points, f) = R @ I_leak(f)

    with ``I_leak(f) = Y_G @ u(f)`` from the reduced network
    ``(Y_L(f) + Y_G) u = i``. Uses the same one-shot assembly as
    :func:`solve_mutual_matrix` (reaction matrix and per-excitation leakage
    columns built once); only the field-point evaluation is generalised. The
    expensive 3D part is therefore frequency-independent and computed once, so
    a frequency sweep over ``I_leak(f)`` is cheap.

    ``world`` must already carry **all** ``nG`` grounding clusters (every
    anchor in ``anchors`` must be a real electrode in ``world``) and the soil
    model. Any current source is ignored — the excitations are applied
    internally, one cluster at a time, exactly as the historic per-excitation
    loop did.

    Parameters
    ----------
    world
        Assembled world holding all ``nG`` grounding clusters and the soil
        model. Sources, if any, are ignored.
    engine
        Engine configuration. ``segment_length`` controls the
        discretisation; ``frequencies`` selects the solved frequency via
        ``frequency_index``; ``image_max_terms`` / ``image_series_tol`` feed
        the 2-layer **self**-kernel (the reaction-matrix assembly), exactly
        as ``Engine.solve`` would.
    anchors
        Length-``nG`` list of electrode names, one per node. Anchor ``j``
        receives the unit current of excitation ``j`` and fills column ``j``
        of ``R``.
    field_points
        ``(M, 3)`` array of ``(x, y, depth)`` evaluation points, decoupled
        from ``nG``: ``M`` may differ from ``nG`` and the points are
        arbitrary (surface or buried). Row ``i`` becomes row ``i`` of ``R``.
    frequency_index
        Index into ``engine.frequencies``. Default 0. Only relevant when
        distributed conductors make the assembled system
        frequency-dependent.
    matrix_min_distance, matrix_max_terms, matrix_tol
        Clamp distance in m and series controls of the field evaluation.
        ``None`` (default) for the series controls takes
        ``engine.image_max_terms`` / ``engine.image_series_tol``, the
        controls :meth:`FieldResult.potential` uses after a solve with the
        same engine (before 2026.11 they were hard-coded to 100 /
        ``1e-6``, review pass 10, 10.25).

    Returns
    -------
    R : np.ndarray, shape (M, nG), complex
        Galvanic Green-function matrix; ``R[i, j]`` is the potential at
        ``field_points[i]`` under unit excitation of cluster ``j``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``world`` has no soil model, holds no electrodes, or
        ``field_points`` does not have shape ``(M, 3)``.
    KeyError
        If an entry of ``anchors`` is not an electrode in ``world``.
    NotImplementedError
        If the soil is a ``MultiLayerSoil`` with three or more layers
        (only homogeneous and 2-layer soils are supported).
    TypeError
        If the soil model type is not supported.

    See Also
    --------
    solve_mutual_matrix : Full ``nG × nG`` mutual grounding-impedance matrix.
    """
    if world.soil is None:
        raise ValueError("World has no soil model.")
    if not world.electrodes:
        raise ValueError("World contains no electrodes.")

    nG = len(anchors)
    field_points = np.asarray(field_points, dtype=float)
    if field_points.ndim != 2 or field_points.shape[1] != 3:
        raise ValueError(
            f"field_points must have shape (M, 3), got {field_points.shape}."
        )

    problem = _prepare(world, engine, frequency_index, where="solve_mutual_field")
    n_segments = len(problem.disc.segments)

    # Per-excitation leakage columns T (no diagonal/self term needed).
    T = np.zeros((n_segments, nG), dtype=complex)
    for j, (_, sc) in enumerate(_unit_excitations(world, problem, list(anchors))):
        T[:, j] = sc

    # Potential at the M field points per excitation (nG) — one kernel pass.
    return _field_of_columns(
        problem,
        field_points,
        T,
        min_distance=matrix_min_distance,
        max_terms=matrix_max_terms,
        tol=matrix_tol,
    )

    solve_mutual_matrix ¶

    solve_mutual_matrix(world: 'World', engine: 'Engine', anchors: list[str], probe_points: ndarray | None = None, *, frequency_index: int = 0, symmetrize: bool = True, offdiag: OffDiagonal = 'galerkin', matrix_min_distance: float = 0.001, matrix_max_terms: int | None = None, matrix_tol: float | None = None) -> np.ndarray

    Full mutual grounding-impedance matrix Z_G in one assembly.

    Column j belongs to 1 A injected into anchors[j]; the other clusters float (zero net current, review pass 10, 10.29), exactly as in Engine.solve() with one source. The segment reaction matrix and the leakage distribution of every excitation are computed once and reused for all entries.

    • Diagonal. Z[j, j] is the cluster impedance of anchors[j], the length-weighted (Galerkin) potential average over every member of its cluster divided by the cluster current — the same reduction as FieldResult.cluster_impedance() after a per-excitation Engine.solve() (equal to round-off). Up to 2026.11 the diagonal was the unweighted mean over the alphabetically first member: +0.150 % for an L-shaped footprint at ds = 2 m, -3.8 … -9.1 % for a rod split at the layer interface (review pass 10, 10.26).
    • Off-diagonal, offdiag="galerkin" (default): the reaction Z[i, j] = T_iᵀ (K + S) T_j of the leakage columns T with the reaction matrix K and the concrete-shell diagonal S. It is the current-weighted potential of cluster i under excitation j — the off-diagonal counterpart of the diagonal, reciprocal to round-off, and the matrix that reproduces a solve of the clusters joined by branches (see Notes).
    • Off-diagonal, offdiag="probe": the potential at probe_points[i] under excitation j, as FieldResult.potential() returns it after a per-excitation solve — the definition of releases up to 0.15.0. A point potential is not the potential of cluster i: the matrix is not reciprocal (Z[i, j] and Z[j, i] differ by up to 35 % in two-layer soil, review pass 10, 10.34), and symmetrize=True averages that asymmetry away. On an AP1-like site (a station and twelve house foundations, ds = 2 m, five soils) the symmetrised probe matrix misses the input impedance of the joined network by -0.15 … -0.88 %, and its off-diagonal entries differ from the galerkin ones by 0.15 … 1.1 % (median) and up to 41 %; the galerkin matrix reproduces the network solve to 1e-12.

    The galerkin off-diagonal is the default of every call since the user decision Q15 of 2026.11. Up to 0.15.0 passing probe_points selected the probe definition; such a call now returns the galerkin matrix and ignores the points with a ProbePointsIgnoredWarning — pass offdiag="probe" to keep the 0.15.0 definition.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    world 'World'

    Assembled world holding all nG grounding clusters and the soil model (homogeneous or two-layer, also as a MultiLayerSoil of at most two distinct layers). Sources, if any, are ignored.

    		 required
    engine 'Engine'

    Engine of the image family (backend="image" and its aliases); segment_length, kernel, image_max_terms and image_series_tol act exactly as in Engine.solve(). frequencies[frequency_index] is the solved frequency.

    		 required
    anchors list[str]

    Length-nG list of electrode names, one per cluster ("gnode").

    		 required
    probe_points ndarray | None

    (nG, 3) array of (x, y, depth) points in m, one per anchor, used by offdiag="probe" only (required there). With offdiag="galerkin" they are ignored, not validated, with a ProbePointsIgnoredWarning.

    		 None
    frequency_index int

    Index into engine.frequencies. Default 0.

    		 0
    symmetrize bool

    If True (default) return 0.5 · (Z + Zᵀ).

    		 True
    offdiag OffDiagonal

    "galerkin" (default) or "probe", see above.

    		 'galerkin'
    matrix_min_distance float

    Clamp distance in m and series controls of the probe-point evaluation (offdiag="probe" only; the galerkin off-diagonal evaluates no field). None (default) for the series controls takes engine.image_max_terms / engine.image_series_tol, the controls FieldResult.potential() uses after a solve with the same engine (before 2026.11 they were hard-coded to 100 / 1e-6, review pass 10, 10.25).

    		 0.001
    matrix_max_terms float

    Clamp distance in m and series controls of the probe-point evaluation (offdiag="probe" only; the galerkin off-diagonal evaluates no field). None (default) for the series controls takes engine.image_max_terms / engine.image_series_tol, the controls FieldResult.potential() uses after a solve with the same engine (before 2026.11 they were hard-coded to 100 / 1e-6, review pass 10, 10.25).

    		 0.001
    matrix_tol float

    Clamp distance in m and series controls of the probe-point evaluation (offdiag="probe" only; the galerkin off-diagonal evaluates no field). None (default) for the series controls takes engine.image_max_terms / engine.image_series_tol, the controls FieldResult.potential() uses after a solve with the same engine (before 2026.11 they were hard-coded to 100 / 1e-6, review pass 10, 10.25).

    		 0.001

    Mutual grounding-impedance matrix in Ω.

    Type Description

    If world has no soil model or no electrodes, if offdiag="probe" comes without probe_points of shape (nG, 3), or if offdiag is unknown.
    BackendCapabilityError

    If the engine's backend is not the image family (a subclass of ValueError; up to 2026.11 the backend was ignored, 10.34).
    ResourceLimitError

    If the problem exceeds engine.max_segments (default groundfield.diagnostics.HARD_LIMIT).
    KeyError

    If an entry of anchors is not an electrode in world.

    Notes

    With the uniform current per owner of the image family, the potential of a cluster is the current-weighted average of its segment potentials. With every other cluster floating, T_iᵀ (K + S) T_j therefore equals the potential of cluster i under excitation j exactly (reciprocity of the reaction matrix), bonded groups and rods through the layer interface included, and (Y_L + Z_G⁻¹) u = i reproduces the solve of the clusters joined by the branches Y_L. With probe off-diagonals it does not (evidence in the 2026.11 changelog).

    def solve_mutual_matrix(
    world: "World",
    engine: "Engine",
    anchors: list[str],
    probe_points: np.ndarray | None = None,
    *,
    frequency_index: int = 0,
    symmetrize: bool = True,
    offdiag: OffDiagonal = "galerkin",
    matrix_min_distance: float = 1e-3,
    matrix_max_terms: int | None = None,
    matrix_tol: float | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Full mutual grounding-impedance matrix ``Z_G`` in one assembly.

    Column ``j`` belongs to 1 A injected into ``anchors[j]``; the other
    clusters float (zero net current, review pass 10, 10.29), exactly as
    in :meth:`Engine.solve` with one source. The segment reaction matrix and the
    leakage distribution of every excitation are computed once and
    reused for all entries.

    * **Diagonal.** ``Z[j, j]`` is the cluster impedance of ``anchors[j]``,
      the length-weighted (Galerkin) potential average over every
      member of its cluster divided by the cluster current — the same
      reduction as :meth:`FieldResult.cluster_impedance` after a
      per-excitation :meth:`Engine.solve` (equal to round-off). Up to
      2026.11 the diagonal was the unweighted mean over the
      alphabetically first member: +0.150 % for an L-shaped footprint
      at ds = 2 m, -3.8 … -9.1 % for a rod split at the layer interface
      (review pass 10, 10.26).
    * **Off-diagonal**, ``offdiag="galerkin"`` (default): the reaction
      ``Z[i, j] = T_iᵀ (K + S) T_j`` of the leakage columns ``T`` with
      the reaction matrix ``K`` and the concrete-shell diagonal ``S``.
      It is the current-weighted potential of cluster ``i`` under
      excitation ``j`` — the off-diagonal counterpart of the diagonal,
      reciprocal to round-off, and the matrix that reproduces a solve
      of the clusters joined by branches (see Notes).
    * **Off-diagonal**, ``offdiag="probe"``: the potential at
      ``probe_points[i]`` under excitation ``j``, as
      :meth:`FieldResult.potential` returns it after a per-excitation
      solve — the definition of releases up to 0.15.0. A point potential
      is not the potential of cluster ``i``: the matrix is not reciprocal
      (``Z[i, j]`` and ``Z[j, i]`` differ by up to 35 % in two-layer soil,
      review pass 10, 10.34), and ``symmetrize=True`` averages that
      asymmetry away. On an AP1-like site (a station and twelve house
      foundations, ds = 2 m, five soils) the symmetrised probe matrix
      misses the input impedance of the joined network by -0.15 …
      -0.88 %, and its off-diagonal entries differ from the galerkin
      ones by 0.15 … 1.1 % (median) and up to 41 %; the galerkin matrix
      reproduces the network solve to 1e-12.

    The galerkin off-diagonal is the default of every call since the
    user decision Q15 of 2026.11. Up to 0.15.0 passing ``probe_points``
    selected the probe definition; such a call now returns the galerkin
    matrix and ignores the points with a :class:`ProbePointsIgnoredWarning`
    — pass ``offdiag="probe"`` to keep the 0.15.0 definition.

    Parameters
    ----------
    world
        Assembled world holding all ``nG`` grounding clusters and the
        soil model (homogeneous or two-layer, also as a
        :class:`~groundfield.soil.MultiLayerSoil` of at most two distinct
        layers). Sources, if any, are ignored.
    engine
        Engine of the image family (``backend="image"`` and its
        aliases); ``segment_length``, ``kernel``, ``image_max_terms`` and
        ``image_series_tol`` act exactly as in :meth:`Engine.solve`.
        ``frequencies[frequency_index]`` is the solved frequency.
    anchors
        Length-``nG`` list of electrode names, one per cluster ("gnode").
    probe_points
        ``(nG, 3)`` array of ``(x, y, depth)`` points in m, one per
        anchor, used by ``offdiag="probe"`` only (required there). With
        ``offdiag="galerkin"`` they are ignored, not validated, with a
        :class:`ProbePointsIgnoredWarning`.
    frequency_index
        Index into ``engine.frequencies``. Default 0.
    symmetrize
        If ``True`` (default) return ``0.5 · (Z + Zᵀ)``.
    offdiag
        ``"galerkin"`` (default) or ``"probe"``, see above.
    matrix_min_distance, matrix_max_terms, matrix_tol
        Clamp distance in m and series controls of the probe-point
        evaluation (``offdiag="probe"`` only; the galerkin off-diagonal
        evaluates no field). ``None`` (default) for the series controls
        takes ``engine.image_max_terms`` / ``engine.image_series_tol``,
        the controls :meth:`FieldResult.potential` uses after a solve with
        the same engine (before 2026.11 they were hard-coded to 100 /
        ``1e-6``, review pass 10, 10.25).

    Returns
    -------
    Z : np.ndarray, shape (nG, nG), complex
        Mutual grounding-impedance matrix in Ω.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``world`` has no soil model or no electrodes, if
        ``offdiag="probe"`` comes without ``probe_points`` of shape
        ``(nG, 3)``, or if ``offdiag`` is unknown.
    BackendCapabilityError
        If the engine's backend is not the image family (a subclass of
        ``ValueError``; up to 2026.11 the backend was ignored, 10.34).
    ResourceLimitError
        If the problem exceeds ``engine.max_segments`` (default
        :data:`groundfield.diagnostics.HARD_LIMIT`).
    KeyError
        If an entry of ``anchors`` is not an electrode in ``world``.

    Warns
    -----
    ProbePointsIgnoredWarning
        If ``probe_points`` are given with ``offdiag="galerkin"`` (the
        default), the call of releases up to 0.15.0.

    Notes
    -----
    With the uniform current per owner of the image family, the
    potential of a cluster is the current-weighted average of its
    segment potentials. With every other cluster floating,
    ``T_iᵀ (K + S) T_j`` therefore equals the potential of cluster ``i``
    under excitation ``j`` exactly (reciprocity of the reaction matrix),
    bonded groups and rods through the layer interface included, and
    ``(Y_L + Z_G⁻¹) u = i`` reproduces the solve of the clusters joined
    by the branches ``Y_L``. With probe off-diagonals it does not
    (evidence in the 2026.11 changelog).
    """
    if world.soil is None:
        raise ValueError("World has no soil model.")
    if not world.electrodes:
        raise ValueError("World contains no electrodes.")
    if offdiag not in _OFFDIAG_CHOICES:
        raise ValueError(f"offdiag must be 'probe' or 'galerkin', got {offdiag!r}.")

    nG = len(anchors)
    if offdiag == "probe":
        if probe_points is None:
            raise ValueError("offdiag='probe' needs probe_points of shape (nG, 3).")
        probe_points = np.asarray(probe_points, dtype=float)
        if probe_points.shape != (nG, 3):
            raise ValueError(
                f"probe_points must have shape ({nG}, 3), got {probe_points.shape}."
            )
    elif probe_points is not None:
        # user decision Q15 (2026-11-08): the galerkin off-diagonal is the
        # default whatever the call; the probe points of a 0.15.0 call are
        # ignored, not rejected, so the call keeps running.
        from groundfield.solver.registry import warn_external

        warn_external(
            "solve_mutual_matrix: probe_points are ignored. The off-diagonal "
            "is offdiag='galerkin' (the default since 2026.11): the reaction "
            "of the leakage distributions, reciprocal, the matrix that "
            "reproduces a solve of the clusters joined by branches. Up to "
            "0.15.0 probe points selected the potential at them instead; "
            "pass offdiag='probe' to keep that definition, or drop "
            "probe_points.",
            ProbePointsIgnoredWarning,
        )
        probe_points = None

    problem = _prepare(world, engine, frequency_index, where="solve_mutual_matrix")
    disc, topo, arrays = problem.disc, problem.topo, problem.arrays
    n_segments = len(disc.segments)
    seg_lengths = arrays.lengths
    Z_seg_full = problem.Z_seg_full

    # ADR-0012 V2 shell augmentation (added to the *diagonal* of the
    # reaction matrix exactly as in ``_solve_cluster_currents`` and the
    # post-solve ``ph`` step).
    shell_diag: np.ndarray | None = None
    if np.any(arrays.shell_coefficients > 0.0):
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            shell_diag = np.where(
                seg_lengths > 0.0,
                arrays.shell_coefficients / seg_lengths,
                0.0,
            )

    # Cluster members per real electrode (== FieldResult.clusters).
    real_set = {e.name for e in world.electrodes}
    cluster_id = topo.cluster_id
    cluster_members: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for ename in (e.name for e in world.electrodes):
        cluster_members[ename] = sorted(
            n
            for n in cluster_id
            if cluster_id[n] == cluster_id[ename] and n in real_set
        )

    T = np.zeros((n_segments, nG), dtype=complex)  # leakage column per excitation
    PH = np.zeros((n_segments, nG), dtype=complex)  # segment potentials per excitation
    Z = np.zeros((nG, nG), dtype=complex)
    excitations = _unit_excitations(world, problem, list(anchors))
    for j, anchor_j in enumerate(anchors):
        elec_total, sc = excitations[j]
        T[:, j] = sc
        if sc.any():
            # Segment potentials as in the post-solve step of the live
            # solver: bulk reaction matrix on the real and imaginary
            # leakage, then the shell augmentation.
            phi_re = Z_seg_full @ sc.real
            phi_im = Z_seg_full @ sc.imag
            if shell_diag is not None:
                phi_re = phi_re + shell_diag * sc.real
                phi_im = phi_im + shell_diag * sc.imag
            PH[:, j] = phi_re + 1j * phi_im
        members = cluster_members.get(anchor_j, [anchor_j])
        Z[j, j] = _cluster_impedance(problem, members, elec_total, PH[:, j])

    if offdiag == "galerkin":
        # Reaction of every pair of leakage columns (bilinear, no
        # conjugation: reciprocity holds for the complex system too).
        Phi = T.T @ PH
    else:
        Phi = _field_of_columns(
            problem,
            probe_points,
            T,
            min_distance=matrix_min_distance,
            max_terms=matrix_max_terms,
            tol=matrix_tol,
        )  # (nG, nG): row i = probe i, column j = excitation j
    off = ~np.eye(nG, dtype=bool)
    Z[off] = Phi[off]

    if symmetrize:
        return 0.5 * (Z + Z.T)
    return Z

    Backend solve functions¶

    Each built-in backend is one solve function, solve_<name>(world, engine), registered in the backend registry. Engine.solve resolves the backend name, checks the capabilities against the world, calls the function and fills the common metadata of the result (CORE_METADATA_KEYS); call the functions directly only to bypass that dispatch, for example in a test. The theory of each backend is on its engine page.

    def solve_image(world: "World", engine: "Engine") -> FieldResult:
    """Image-charge solver for homogeneous soil.

    Runs the shared image-family pipeline
    (:mod:`groundfield.solver._pipeline`) with the half-space Green's
    function.

    Parameters
    ----------
    world
        World whose ``soil`` must be a :class:`HomogeneousSoil`.
    engine
        Engine configuration; relevant fields are ``segment_length``,
        ``frequencies`` and ``earth_inductive_model``.

    Returns
    -------
    FieldResult
        Node potentials and leakage currents per frequency, point
        sources and metadata.

    Raises
    ------
    BackendCapabilityError
        If the soil is a layered model (:meth:`Engine.solve
        <groundfield.solver.engine.Engine.solve>` forwards those to
        ``image_2layer``). Before 2026.11 this was a :class:`TypeError`.
    TypeError
        If ``world.soil`` is no soil model.
    ValueError
        If the world has no electrodes, or the geometry fails a
        discretisation guard (thin wire, burial depth).
    """
    if isinstance(world.soil, (TwoLayerSoil, MultiLayerSoil)):
        from groundfield.solver.registry import BackendCapabilityError

        raise BackendCapabilityError(
            f"Backend 'image' solves homogeneous soil; got a "
            f"{type(world.soil).__name__}. Engine(backend='image').solve "
            "forwards layered soils to image_2layer (at most two distinct "
            "layers); use backend='mom_sommerfeld' for three or more."
        )
    if not isinstance(world.soil, HomogeneousSoil):
        raise TypeError(
            "Backend 'image' requires a HomogeneousSoil. "
            f"Got: {type(world.soil).__name__}."
        )
    if not world.electrodes:
        raise ValueError("World contains no electrodes.")
    if engine.kernel is None:
        # A direct call resolves the default like Engine.solve (10.28).
        engine = engine._with(kernel=DEFAULT_KERNEL)
    green = _HalfSpaceGreen(world.soil.rho, engine.kernel)
    return solve_image_family(world, engine, green, stacklevel=3)

    solve_image_2layer ¶

    solve_image_2layer(world: 'World', engine: 'Engine', *, max_terms: int | None = None, tol: float | None = None, far_field: str | None = None) -> FieldResult

    Image-charge solver for 2-layer soil (Tagg / Sunde).

    Runs the shared image-family pipeline (groundfield.solver._pipeline) with the two-layer Green's function.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    world 'World'

    World whose soil is a TwoLayerSoil. Electrodes in the upper layer use the Tagg/Sunde series; geometries reaching the interface use the ADR-0007 Sommerfeld path.

    		 required
    engine 'Engine'

    Engine configuration. engine.segment_length controls the discretisation as in the homogeneous backend.

    		 required
    max_terms int | None

    Maximum number of series terms; None (default) takes engine.image_max_terms.

    		 None
    tol float | None

    Series truncation: stop as soon as the geometric tail bound \(|K|^{n+1}/(1-|K|)\) falls below tol (dimensionless); None (default) takes engine.image_series_tol.

    		 None
    far_field str | None

    Form of the far images with the line kernel, "quadrupole" or "point"; None (default) takes engine.image_far_field.

    		 None

    Returns:

    Type Description
    FieldResult

    Result object. FieldResult.metadata exposes diagnostic fields (K, rho_1, rho_2, h_1, n_terms_used, converged, series_used, series).

    Raises:

    Type Description
    BackendCapabilityError

    If the soil is a HomogeneousSoil or a MultiLayerSoil with three or more distinct layers (a stack with at most two is solved as the equivalent two-layer soil). Before 2026.11 both raised TypeError.
    TypeError

    If world.soil is no soil model.
    ValueError

    If the world has no electrodes, if far_field is not one of "quadrupole" and "point" (audit W3R2A-02; before, every other value ran the point form and was recorded as given), or if the geometry fails a discretisation guard (thin wire, burial depth).

    Warns:

    Type Description
    SeriesTruncationWarning

    If the series is used and reaches max_terms before tol.

    """Image-charge solver for 2-layer soil (Tagg / Sunde).

    Runs the shared image-family pipeline
    (:mod:`groundfield.solver._pipeline`) with the two-layer Green's
    function.

    Parameters
    ----------
    world

        the upper layer use the Tagg/Sunde series; geometries reaching
        the interface use the ADR-0007 Sommerfeld path.
    engine
        Engine configuration. ``engine.segment_length`` controls the
        discretisation as in the homogeneous backend.
    max_terms
        Maximum number of series terms; ``None`` (default) takes
        ``engine.image_max_terms``.
    tol
        Series truncation: stop as soon as the geometric tail bound
        $|K|^{n+1}/(1-|K|)$ falls below ``tol`` (dimensionless);
        ``None`` (default) takes ``engine.image_series_tol``.
    far_field
        Form of the far images with the line kernel, ``"quadrupole"`` or
        ``"point"``; ``None`` (default) takes ``engine.image_far_field``.

    Returns
    -------
    FieldResult
        Result object. :attr:`FieldResult.metadata` exposes diagnostic
        fields (``K``, ``rho_1``, ``rho_2``, ``h_1``, ``n_terms_used``,
        ``converged``, ``series_used``, ``series``).

    Raises
    ------
    BackendCapabilityError
        If the soil is a :class:`HomogeneousSoil` or a
        :class:`~groundfield.soil.models.MultiLayerSoil` with three or
        more distinct layers (a stack with at most two is solved as the
        equivalent two-layer soil). Before 2026.11 both raised
        :class:`TypeError`.
    TypeError
        If ``world.soil`` is no soil model.
    ValueError
        If the world has no electrodes, if ``far_field`` is not one of
        ``"quadrupole"`` and ``"point"`` (audit W3R2A-02; before, every other
        value ran the point form and was recorded as given), or if the
        geometry fails a discretisation guard (thin wire, burial depth).

    Warns
    -----
    SeriesTruncationWarning
        If the series is used and reaches ``max_terms`` before ``tol``.
    """
    if isinstance(world.soil, MultiLayerSoil):
        # Audit round 1, A1-numerics F09: the registry accepts a layer
        # stack that merges to at most two layers; solve it as the
        # equivalent TwoLayerSoil instead of raising a bare TypeError.
        world = world.model_copy(update={"soil": _as_two_layer(world.soil)})
    if isinstance(world.soil, HomogeneousSoil):
        from groundfield.solver.registry import BackendCapabilityError

        raise BackendCapabilityError(
            "Backend 'image_2layer' solves two-layer soil; got a "
            "HomogeneousSoil. Use backend='image' (Engine(backend='image')"
            ".solve dispatches by soil model)."
        )
    if not isinstance(world.soil, TwoLayerSoil):
        raise TypeError(
            "Backend 'image_2layer' requires a TwoLayerSoil. "
            f"Got: {type(world.soil).__name__}."
        )
    if not world.electrodes:
        raise ValueError("World contains no electrodes.")

    soil: TwoLayerSoil = world.soil
    _log.info(
        "image_2layer: rho_1=%.1f, rho_2=%.1f, h_1=%.2f, K=%.4f",
        soil.rho_1,
        soil.rho_2,
        soil.h_1,
        soil.reflection_coefficient,
    )
    if max_terms is None:
        max_terms = engine.image_max_terms
    if tol is None:
        tol = engine.image_series_tol
    if far_field is None:
        far_field = engine.image_far_field
    if engine.kernel is None:
        # The backend's preferred kernel (Engine.kernel = None, 10.28).
        engine = engine._with(kernel=DEFAULT_KERNEL)
    green = _TwoLayerGreen(
        soil, max_terms, tol, engine.segment_length, engine.kernel, far_field
    )
    owner_interfaces = None
    if _crosses_interface(world, _owner_interfaces(soil)):
        # One owner per (electrode, layer) for rods through h_1 (10.15), on
        # top of the one owner per straight wire of every world (Q30).
        owner_interfaces = _owner_interfaces(soil)
    return solve_image_family(
        world, engine, green, stacklevel=3, owner_interfaces=owner_interfaces
    )

    def solve_mom(
    world: World,
    engine: Engine,
    *,
    two_layer_max_terms: int | None = None,
    two_layer_tol: float | None = None,
) -> FieldResult:
    """Point-matching method-of-moments backend.

    Supports :class:`HomogeneousSoil`, :class:`TwoLayerSoil` and a
    :class:`MultiLayerSoil` whose canonical stack has at most two layers
    (10.48). The Green's-function kernel is taken from the matching
    image backend; only the resolution scheme (one current per segment,
    point matching at the segment midpoints, instead of one uniform
    current per straight wire of an electrode) differs. Clusters without a source float
    (zero net current, 10.29). Concrete-encased electrodes carry the
    per-segment shell term of ADR-0012 (since 2026.11). See the module
    docstring for the accuracy of the scheme and the shared solve flow.

    Parameters
    ----------
    world
        World to evaluate.
    engine
        Engine configuration; ``engine.segment_length`` (m) controls the
        discretisation.
    two_layer_max_terms, two_layer_tol
        Truncation parameters for the Tagg/Sunde series (term count,
        dimensionless tail bound), only used for two-layer soil.
        ``None`` (default) takes ``engine.image_max_terms`` /
        ``engine.image_series_tol``, so the engine knob reaches this
        backend consistently with ``image_2layer``.

    Returns
    -------
    FieldResult
        Result object compatible with :class:`FieldResult` from the
        image backends. ``metadata['solver']`` is ``'point_matching'``
        (``'galerkin'`` up to 0.15.0, although the scheme was the
        same).

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the world has no electrodes, or a segment lies partly above
        the soil surface.
    BackendCapabilityError
        For a :class:`MultiLayerSoil` with three or more distinct layers
        (a :class:`TypeError` before 2026.11).
    TypeError
        If ``world.soil`` is no soil model.
    """
    if not world.electrodes:
        raise ValueError("World contains no electrodes.")
    if not isinstance(world.soil, (HomogeneousSoil, TwoLayerSoil, MultiLayerSoil)):
        raise TypeError(
            "Backend 'mom' supports HomogeneousSoil, TwoLayerSoil and "
            "MultiLayerSoil stacks with at most two distinct layers. "
            f"Got: {type(world.soil).__name__}."
        )
    # Review pass 10, 10.48: solve the canonical soil — a MultiLayerSoil
    # whose adjacent layers share a resistivity is a two-layer (or
    # homogeneous) soil, and a TwoLayerSoil without contrast is
    # homogeneous.
    soil = canonical_soil(world.soil)
    if isinstance(soil, MultiLayerSoil):
        from groundfield.solver.registry import BackendCapabilityError

        raise BackendCapabilityError(
            "Backend 'mom' supports at most two distinct soil layers; this "
            f"MultiLayerSoil has {len(soil.layers)}. Use "
            "backend='mom_sommerfeld' for n >= 3 soils."
        )
    if two_layer_max_terms is None:
        two_layer_max_terms = engine.image_max_terms
    if two_layer_tol is None:
        two_layer_tol = engine.image_series_tol
    _log.info(
        "mom: soil=%s, segment_length=%.3f",
        type(soil).__name__,
        engine.segment_length,
    )
    green = _MomGreen(soil, two_layer_max_terms, two_layer_tol)
    return solve_point_matching(world, engine, green, stacklevel=3)

    solve_mom_sommerfeld ¶

    solve_mom_sommerfeld(world: World, engine: Engine, *, lambda_max_factor: float = 200.0, epsabs: float = 1e-09, epsrel: float = 1e-07, max_osc_panels: int = _MAX_OSC_PANELS, tabulate: bool = True) -> FieldResult

    Point-matching MoM with direct Sommerfeld quadrature for layered soil.

    The discretisation and the linear solve are those of mom (point matching at the segment midpoints, point-source near field, source-free clusters floating), run through the shared solve pipeline (10.75). Every off-diagonal reaction-matrix entry is the Sommerfeld kernel of sommerfeld_kernel_value(), i.e. the closed-form direct pair plus a numerically integrated reflected remainder; no image series and no fit enter the off-diagonal kernel. For \(n = 2\) the diagonal is the Tagg/Sunde series diagonal of mom, so on two-layer soil this backend reproduces mom and checks the kernel, not the scheme; for \(n \ge 3\) distinct layers it is the only integral-equation backend.

    Cost (review pass 10, 10.61): pairs that share a depth pair and a horizontal distance share one quadrature, which halves the work of every world and collapses it for regular geometries. For \(n \ge 3\) the reflected remainder of a depth group with many distinct distances is tabulated on log-spaced nodes and interpolated (tabulate=True, the default): about \(10^{-7}\) relative error of the kernel at the verification points and below \(10^{-6}\) on the reaction matrix of the benchmark grid B12, for a cost that no longer grows with the number of pairs. tabulate=False evaluates every distinct pair by quadrature (the kernel reference). For \(n = 2\) every pair is evaluated by quadrature: this backend is the kernel check of the closed-form series there.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    world World

    World to evaluate.

    		 required
    engine Engine

    Engine configuration.

    		 required
    lambda_max_factor float

    Truncation of the remainder quadrature in units of the remainder decay length \(1 / d_{\text{rem}}\); saturates at 60. See sommerfeld_kernel_value() for the delegated \(n = 2\) cross-layer path.

    		 200.0
    epsabs float

    Convergence thresholds of the remainder quadrature (absolute in 1/m, relative).

    		 1e-09
    epsrel float

    Convergence thresholds of the remainder quadrature (absolute in 1/m, relative).

    		 1e-09
    max_osc_panels int

    Budget for the \(J_0\) half-period panel family.

    		 _MAX_OSC_PANELS
    tabulate bool

    Depth-group tabulation of the reflected kernel for \(n \ge 3\) (see above).

    		 True

    Returns:

    Type Description
    FieldResult

    metadata['converged'] (one bool) and metadata['converged_per_frequency'] report the quadrature and series convergence (10.47); metadata['kernel_tabulation'] the tabulation counters and the largest relative error at its verification points.

    Warns:

    Type Description
    SommerfeldConvergenceWarning

    Once per solve, if any reaction-matrix entry's remainder quadrature failed to converge.
    Notes

    The quadrature keywords are reachable through Engine.options["mom_sommerfeld"] (MomSommerfeldOptions); the signature defaults equal the option defaults, so a direct call without keywords behaves exactly like solve().

    Raises:

    Type Description
    TypeError

    If the soil is not a HomogeneousSoil, TwoLayerSoil or MultiLayerSoil.
    ValueError

    If the world has no electrodes.

    def solve_mom_sommerfeld(
    world: World,
    engine: Engine,
    *,
    lambda_max_factor: float = 200.0,
    epsabs: float = 1e-9,
    epsrel: float = 1e-7,
    max_osc_panels: int = _MAX_OSC_PANELS,
    tabulate: bool = True,
) -> FieldResult:
    """Point-matching MoM with direct Sommerfeld quadrature for layered soil.

    The discretisation and the linear solve are those of ``mom`` (point
    matching at the segment midpoints, point-source near field,
    source-free clusters floating), run through the shared solve
    pipeline (10.75). Every off-diagonal reaction-matrix entry is the
    Sommerfeld kernel of :func:`sommerfeld_kernel_value`, i.e. the
    closed-form direct pair plus a numerically integrated reflected
    remainder; no image series and no fit enter the off-diagonal
    kernel. For $n = 2$ the diagonal is the Tagg/Sunde series diagonal
    of ``mom``, so on two-layer soil this backend reproduces ``mom`` and
    checks the kernel, not the scheme; for $n \\ge 3$ distinct layers it
    is the only integral-equation backend.

    Cost (review pass 10, 10.61): pairs that share a depth pair and a
    horizontal distance share one quadrature, which halves the work of
    every world and collapses it for regular geometries. For
    $n \\ge 3$ the reflected remainder of a depth group with many
    distinct distances is tabulated on log-spaced nodes and interpolated
    (``tabulate=True``, the default): about $10^{-7}$ relative error of
    the kernel at the verification points and below $10^{-6}$ on the
    reaction matrix of the benchmark grid B12, for a cost that no longer
    grows with the number of pairs. ``tabulate=False`` evaluates every
    distinct pair by quadrature (the kernel reference). For $n = 2$
    every pair is evaluated by quadrature: this backend is the kernel
    check of the closed-form series there.

    Parameters
    ----------
    world
        World to evaluate.
    engine
        Engine configuration.
    lambda_max_factor
        Truncation of the remainder quadrature in units of the
        remainder decay length $1 / d_{\\text{rem}}$; saturates at
        60. See :func:`sommerfeld_kernel_value` for the delegated
        $n = 2$ cross-layer path.
    epsabs, epsrel
        Convergence thresholds of the remainder quadrature (absolute
        in 1/m, relative).
    max_osc_panels
        Budget for the $J_0$ half-period panel family.
    tabulate
        Depth-group tabulation of the reflected kernel for $n \\ge 3$
        (see above).

    Returns
    -------
    FieldResult
        ``metadata['converged']`` (one bool) and
        ``metadata['converged_per_frequency']`` report the quadrature
        and series convergence (10.47);
        ``metadata['kernel_tabulation']`` the tabulation counters and
        the largest relative error at its verification points.

    Warns
    -----
    SommerfeldConvergenceWarning
        Once per solve, if any reaction-matrix entry's remainder
        quadrature failed to converge.

    Notes
    -----
    The quadrature keywords are reachable through
    ``Engine.options["mom_sommerfeld"]``
    (:class:`~groundfield.solver.registry.MomSommerfeldOptions`); the
    signature defaults equal the option defaults, so a direct call
    without keywords behaves exactly like
    :meth:`~groundfield.solver.engine.Engine.solve`.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If the soil is not a :class:`HomogeneousSoil`,
        :class:`TwoLayerSoil` or :class:`MultiLayerSoil`.
    ValueError
        If the world has no electrodes.
    """
    if not isinstance(world.soil, (HomogeneousSoil, TwoLayerSoil, MultiLayerSoil)):
        raise TypeError(
            "Backend 'mom_sommerfeld' supports HomogeneousSoil, "
            "TwoLayerSoil, and MultiLayerSoil. "
            f"Got: {type(world.soil).__name__}."
        )
    if not world.electrodes:
        raise ValueError("World contains no electrodes.")
    green = _SommerfeldGreen(
        world.soil,
        lambda_max_factor=lambda_max_factor,
        epsabs=epsabs,
        epsrel=epsrel,
        max_osc_panels=max_osc_panels,
        max_terms=engine.image_max_terms,
        tol=engine.image_series_tol,
        tabulate=tabulate,
    )
    _log.info(
        "mom_sommerfeld: n_layers=%d, segment_length=%.3f, lam_max_fac=%.1f",
        green.stack.n_layers,
        engine.segment_length,
        lambda_max_factor,
    )
    return solve_point_matching(world, engine, green, stacklevel=3)

    sommerfeld_kernel_value ¶

    sommerfeld_kernel_value(stack: LayerStack, s: float, z: float, z_s: float, *, lambda_max_factor: float = 200.0, epsabs: float = 1e-09, epsrel: float = 1e-07, max_osc_panels: int = _MAX_OSC_PANELS, issues: list[_QuadratureIssue] | None = None) -> float

    Evaluate the layered-soil Sommerfeld kernel at one point.

    Returns the full top-layer kernel $$ G(s, z, z_s) \;=\; \int_0^{\infty} \frac{e^{-\lambda |z - z_s|} + \Gamma_1 e^{-\lambda (2 h_1 - |z - z_s|)} + e^{-\lambda (z + z_s)} + \Gamma_1 e^{-\lambda (2 h_1 - z - z_s)}} {1 - \Gamma_1(\lambda)\, e^{-2 \lambda h_1}} J_0(\lambda s)\, d\lambda , $$ i.e. both image families plus the full multiple-reflection multiplier between the free surface (\(R_{\text{air}} = +1\)) and the layer interface. The potential of a point source \(I\) is then ρ_1 · I · G / (4 π).

    The integral is not evaluated by a bare real-axis quadrature: the two \(\Gamma_1 \to 0\) terms (which converge only through the oscillation of \(J_0\) and are the reason the pre-0.15.0 implementation could return a negative value) are taken from Lipschitz' integral \(\int_0^\infty e^{-\lambda d} J_0(\lambda s) d\lambda = (s^2 + d^2)^{-1/2}\), so that $$ G = \frac{1}{\sqrt{s^2 + (z - z_s)^2}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{s^2 + (z + z_s)^2}} + G_{\text{refl}}, $$ and only the exponentially decaying reflected remainder \(G_{\text{refl}}\) is integrated numerically — see _reflected_integral().

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    stack LayerStack

    Layer stack.

    		 required
    s float

    Cylindrical radius \(s = \sqrt{(x - x_s)^2 + (y - y_s)^2}\) in metres.

    		 required
    z float

    Field-point depth and source depth (positive into the soil).

    		 required
    z_s float

    Field-point depth and source depth (positive into the soil).

    		 required
    lambda_max_factor float

    Truncation of the remainder quadrature, in units of \(1 / d_{\text{rem}}\), where \(d_{\text{rem}}\) is the decay length of the remainder (not, as before 0.15.0, a characteristic length of the geometry). The discarded tail is bounded by \(e^{-\texttt{lambda\_max\_factor}}\); the factor saturates at 60 (\(\sim 10^{-26}\)), so raising it beyond the default cannot change the result.

    On the delegated \(n = 2\) cross-layer path (\(z > h_1\) or \(z_s > h_1\), forwarded to groundfield.coupling.layered_green.two_layer_real_space_kernel()) the keyword is measured in units of a geometric characteristic length instead. Since the F14 fix of 0.15.0 that kernel adds every image term it does not resolve back in closed form, so the factor is only an upper bound there as well: values from 30 to 20 000 change the delegated kernel by at most 1.3e-8 and raise no warning (review pass 10; the pre-0.15.0 advice to lower the factor on that path is obsolete).

    		 200.0
    epsabs float

    Absolute / relative thresholds of the grid-refinement convergence test of the remainder quadrature. epsrel is measured against the magnitude of the whole kernel. They are not forwarded to the delegated \(n = 2\) cross-layer path, which carries its own fixed-order grid.

    		 1e-09
    epsrel float

    Absolute / relative thresholds of the grid-refinement convergence test of the remainder quadrature. epsrel is measured against the magnitude of the whole kernel. They are not forwarded to the delegated \(n = 2\) cross-layer path, which carries its own fixed-order grid.

    		 1e-09
    max_osc_panels int

    Budget for the half-period panel family that resolves the \(J_0(\lambda s)\) oscillation, default 200 000 panels (× 12 Gauss nodes). Only binds for \(s / d_{\text{rem}} \gtrsim 1.9 \cdot 10^{4}\), i.e. a centimetre-thin intermediate layer combined with a kilometre-scale horizontal separation; there the coverage is incomplete, a SommerfeldConvergenceWarning is raised and raising this budget is the remedy (cost grows linearly).

    		 _MAX_OSC_PANELS
    issues list[_QuadratureIssue] | None

    Optional collector for non-convergence diagnostics; see _reflected_integral(). Used by _build_Z_sommerfeld() to aggregate \(O(N^2)\) warnings into one.

    		 None

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    G float

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    For \(n \ge 3\) with \(z > h_1\) or \(z_s > h_1\): the expression above is a top-layer form, so the kernel refuses instead of silently returning a diverging number (before 0.15.0 it returned \(\approx -2 \cdot 10^{127}\) there).

    Warns:

    Type Description
    SommerfeldConvergenceWarning

    If the remainder quadrature does not reach the requested tolerance. The returned value is then not converged and its sign may be wrong.
    Notes

    Limits and special cases:

    • stack.n_layers == 1 (homogeneous, \(\Gamma_1 \equiv 0\)): short-circuited to \(1/r + 1/r_{\text{img}}\), bit-exact.
    • \(\rho_1 = \rho_2\) in a declared 2-layer stack (\(K_1 = 0\), hence \(\Gamma_1 \equiv 0\)): the reflected remainder is identically zero, so the same closed form is returned bit-exact. This is the strongest available accuracy test of the backend.
    • stack.n_layers == 2 with \(z > h_1\) or \(z_s > h_1\): delegated to groundfield.coupling.layered_green.two_layer_real_space_kernel(), which solves the cross-layer spectral matching.

    Distances are floored at 1 mm (_MIN_DISTANCE), consistently with the homogeneous image backend, so the coincident-point limit stays finite.

    def sommerfeld_kernel_value(
    stack: LayerStack,
    s: float,
    z: float,
    z_s: float,
    *,
    lambda_max_factor: float = 200.0,
    epsabs: float = 1e-9,
    epsrel: float = 1e-7,
    max_osc_panels: int = _MAX_OSC_PANELS,
    issues: list[_QuadratureIssue] | None = None,
) -> float:
    """Evaluate the layered-soil Sommerfeld kernel at one point.

    Returns the full top-layer kernel
    $$
    G(s, z, z_s) \\;=\\; \\int_0^{\\infty}
    \\frac{e^{-\\lambda |z - z_s|}
         + \\Gamma_1 e^{-\\lambda (2 h_1 - |z - z_s|)}
         + e^{-\\lambda (z + z_s)}
         + \\Gamma_1 e^{-\\lambda (2 h_1 - z - z_s)}}
         {1 - \\Gamma_1(\\lambda)\\, e^{-2 \\lambda h_1}}
    J_0(\\lambda s)\\, d\\lambda ,
    $$
    i.e. both image families plus the full multiple-reflection
    multiplier between the free surface ($R_{\\text{air}} = +1$)
    and the layer interface. The potential of a point source $I$
    is then ``ρ_1 · I · G / (4 π)``.

    The integral is **not** evaluated by a bare real-axis quadrature:
    the two $\\Gamma_1 \\to 0$ terms (which converge only through
    the oscillation of $J_0$ and are the reason the pre-0.15.0
    implementation could return a negative value) are taken from
    Lipschitz' integral
    $\\int_0^\\infty e^{-\\lambda d} J_0(\\lambda s) d\\lambda
    = (s^2 + d^2)^{-1/2}$, so that
    $$
    G = \\frac{1}{\\sqrt{s^2 + (z - z_s)^2}}
      + \\frac{1}{\\sqrt{s^2 + (z + z_s)^2}}
      + G_{\\text{refl}},
    $$
    and only the exponentially decaying reflected remainder
    $G_{\\text{refl}}$ is integrated numerically — see
    :func:`_reflected_integral`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    stack
        Layer stack.
    s
        Cylindrical radius $s = \\sqrt{(x - x_s)^2 + (y - y_s)^2}$
        in metres.
    z, z_s
        Field-point depth and source depth (positive into the soil).
    lambda_max_factor
        Truncation of the *remainder* quadrature, in units of
        $1 / d_{\\text{rem}}$, where $d_{\\text{rem}}$ is the
        decay length of the remainder (not, as before 0.15.0, a
        characteristic length of the geometry). The discarded tail is
        bounded by $e^{-\\texttt{lambda\\_max\\_factor}}$; the factor
        saturates at 60 ($\\sim 10^{-26}$), so raising it beyond
        the default cannot change the result.

        On the delegated $n = 2$ cross-layer path ($z > h_1$ or
        $z_s > h_1$, forwarded to
        :func:`groundfield.coupling.layered_green.two_layer_real_space_kernel`)
        the keyword is measured in units of a *geometric*
        characteristic length instead. Since the F14 fix of 0.15.0
        that kernel adds every image term it does not resolve back in
        closed form, so the factor is only an upper bound there as
        well: values from 30 to 20 000 change the delegated kernel by
        at most 1.3e-8 and raise no warning (review pass 10; the
        pre-0.15.0 advice to *lower* the factor on that path is
        obsolete).
    epsabs, epsrel
        Absolute / relative thresholds of the grid-refinement
        convergence test of the remainder quadrature. ``epsrel`` is
        measured against the magnitude of the *whole* kernel. They are
        **not** forwarded to the delegated $n = 2$ cross-layer path,
        which carries its own fixed-order grid.
    max_osc_panels
        Budget for the half-period panel family that resolves the
        $J_0(\\lambda s)$ oscillation, default 200 000 panels
        (× 12 Gauss nodes). Only binds for
        $s / d_{\\text{rem}} \\gtrsim 1.9 \\cdot 10^{4}$, i.e. a
        centimetre-thin intermediate layer combined with a
        kilometre-scale horizontal separation; there the coverage is
        incomplete, a :class:`SommerfeldConvergenceWarning` is raised
        and raising this budget is the remedy (cost grows linearly).
    issues
        Optional collector for non-convergence diagnostics; see
        :func:`_reflected_integral`. Used by
        :func:`_build_Z_sommerfeld` to aggregate $O(N^2)$ warnings
        into one.

    Returns
    -------
    G : float

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        For $n \\ge 3$ with $z > h_1$ or $z_s > h_1$: the
        expression above is a top-layer form, so the kernel refuses
        instead of silently returning a diverging number (before
        0.15.0 it returned $\\approx -2 \\cdot 10^{127}$ there).

    Warns
    -----
    SommerfeldConvergenceWarning
        If the remainder quadrature does not reach the requested
        tolerance. The returned value is then not converged and its
        sign may be wrong.

    Notes
    -----
    Limits and special cases:

    - ``stack.n_layers == 1`` (homogeneous, $\\Gamma_1 \\equiv 0$):
      short-circuited to $1/r + 1/r_{\\text{img}}$, bit-exact.
    - $\\rho_1 = \\rho_2$ in a declared 2-layer stack
      ($K_1 = 0$, hence $\\Gamma_1 \\equiv 0$): the reflected
      remainder is identically zero, so the same closed form is
      returned bit-exact. This is the strongest available accuracy
      test of the backend.
    - ``stack.n_layers == 2`` with $z > h_1$ or $z_s > h_1$:
      delegated to
      :func:`groundfield.coupling.layered_green.two_layer_real_space_kernel`,
      which solves the cross-layer spectral matching.

    Distances are floored at 1 mm (``_MIN_DISTANCE``), consistently
    with the homogeneous ``image`` backend, so the coincident-point
    limit stays finite.
    """
    # Homogeneous shortcut.
    if stack.n_layers <= 1:
        r = np.sqrt(s**2 + (z - z_s) ** 2)
        r_img = np.sqrt(s**2 + (z + z_s) ** 2)
        return float(1.0 / max(r, _MIN_DISTANCE) + 1.0 / max(r_img, _MIN_DISTANCE))

    # ADR-0006 Phase B: 2-layer soil with cross-layer source/observer.
    # Delegate to coupling.layered_green which solves the full 2-layer
    # spectral matching for any (z_layer, z_s_layer) combination. The
    # caller multiplies by rho_1/(4π); the layered_green kernel
    # internally carries the source-layer rho factor, so we divide
    # out rho_1 here to match the existing convention.
    if stack.n_layers == 2 and (z > stack.h[0] or z_s > stack.h[0]):
        from groundfield.coupling.layered_green import (
            two_layer_real_space_kernel,
        )

        # ``lambda_max_factor`` is measured in units of a geometric
        # length here (1/d_rem on the top-layer path below). It is
        # forwarded verbatim: since F14 (0.15.0) the delegated kernel
        # adds the unresolved image terms back in closed form, so the
        # factor is an upper bound only (30 ... 20 000 change the
        # kernel by <= 1.3e-8, review pass 10).
        rho_1_local = float(stack.rhos[0])
        rho_2_local = float(stack.rhos[1])
        h_1_local = float(stack.h[0])
        # Distances floored at 1 mm like every other branch here: the
        # closed-form 1/R terms of the delegated kernel are clamped at
        # min(h_1/200, 1 mm) instead of h_1/200 (audit A3S-01).
        G_phys = two_layer_real_space_kernel(
            s=s,
            z=z,
            z_s=z_s,
            rho_1=rho_1_local,
            rho_2=rho_2_local,
            h_1=h_1_local,
            lambda_max_factor=lambda_max_factor,
            min_distance=_MIN_DISTANCE,
        )
        # G_phys has rho/2·(1/r + ...) structure; the existing caller
        # forms Z = rho_1/(4π)·G_old, so we want G_old = 2·G_phys/rho_1.
        return float(2.0 * G_phys / rho_1_local)

    # Layered case — full top-layer Sommerfeld form.
    #
    # The complete Green's function of a top-layer source observed in the
    # top layer combines four exponentials, each propagated through the
    # multiple-reflection multiplier 1/(1 - Γ_1(λ)·e^{-2λh_1}):
    #
    #   ξ(λ) = (e^{-λ|z-z_s|} + Γ_1·e^{-λ(2h_1-|z-z_s|)}
    #         + e^{-λ(z+z_s)}  + Γ_1·e^{-λ(2h_1-z-z_s)})
    #          / (1 - Γ_1(λ)·e^{-2λh_1})
    #
    # In the limits Γ_1 → 0 this reduces to the homogeneous form
    # e^{-λ|z-z_s|} + e^{-λ(z+z_s)}; for Γ_1 = K_1 = const it expands
    # into the classical Tagg/Sunde geometric series in K_1^n at images
    # ±2nh_1 ± z_s.
    #
    # The two Γ_1 → 0 terms are the conditionally convergent part of
    # the integral and are taken from Lipschitz' integral in closed
    # form; only the decaying reflected remainder is quadratured.
    h_top = float(stack.h[0])
    z_tol = 1e-9 * max(h_top, 1.0)
    if z > h_top + z_tol or z_s > h_top + z_tol:
        # Only reachable for n >= 3 (n == 2 is handled above). The
        # top-layer form is not valid below the interface; before
        # 0.15.0 it silently returned a diverging number (≈ -2e127).
        raise ValueError(
            "mom_sommerfeld: the n>=3 top-layer Sommerfeld kernel "
            "requires both the field point and the source inside the "
            f"upper layer (got z = {z:.4f} m, z_s = {z_s:.4f} m, "
            f"h_1 = {h_top:.4f} m). Use backend='image_2layer' for "
            "cross-layer geometries on a 2-layer soil."
        )
    abs_dz = abs(z - z_s)
    z_plus = z + z_s
    r = float(np.hypot(s, abs_dz))
    r_img = float(np.hypot(s, z_plus))
    G_direct = 1.0 / max(r, _MIN_DISTANCE) + 1.0 / max(r_img, _MIN_DISTANCE)

    G_refl = _reflected_integral(
        stack,
        s,
        abs_dz,
        z_plus,
        lambda_max_factor=lambda_max_factor,
        epsabs=epsabs,
        epsrel=epsrel,
        reference=G_direct,
        max_osc_panels=max_osc_panels,
        issues=issues,
    )
    return float(G_direct + G_refl)

    solve_fem ¶

    solve_fem(world: 'World', engine: 'Engine', *, refinement: int = 0, extrapolate: bool = True, r_far_factor: float = 1000.0, far_field: str = 'robin', max_nodes: int = 2000000, max_nodes_3d: int = 2000000, max_ports_3d: int = 100, model: str = 'auto', source_radius: float | None = None, growth: float = 0.5, concrete_resistivity: float | None = None, _concrete_mesh: float | None = None, n_radial: int | None = None, n_axial: int | None = None, z_far_factor: float | None = None) -> FieldResult

    Conforming finite-element solve (see the module docstring).

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    world 'World'

    World to solve, any horizontally layered soil, bare or encased electrodes (see model).

    		 required
    engine 'Engine'

    Engine; its frequencies, earth_inductive_model (conductor branches) and segment_length (the display segments that carry the leakage distribution of the result) are used.

    		 required
    refinement int

    Refinement level of the coarser of the two meshes (axisymmetric model: each level bisects every interval of the graded mesh lines, about four times the nodes; 3-D model: about eight times). 0 (default) gives a port resistance within about 1e-4 of the converged value for coaxial rods and rings. A ring wire that an interface cuts or comes within 1.05 radii of: within 5.1e-5 of an independent boundary-element model of the solid torus at layer contrasts of 3 ... 1000, on either side, cut or touching (60 cases of audit W4R2A's sweep, estimates 3.9e-4 ... 1.5e-3), and -8.5e-4 touching a layer 10 000 times more conductive (estimate 5.3e-3); refinement=1 within 1.9e-5 and 3.3e-4 (evidence fw4r2a/e05, e08).

    		 0
    extrapolate bool

    Solve at refinement and refinement + 1 and extrapolate the port conductance matrix with the second order (default). False solves the level refinement alone; its resistance usually lies below the converged value (see Notes) and metadata["fem_error_estimate"] is NaN (one level has no estimate).

    		 True
    r_far_factor float

    Size of the truncation box in characteristic lengths (the electrodes' size, or the depth of the deepest interface times the layer contrast if larger); dimensionless, default 1000.

    		 1000.0
    far_field str

    "robin" (default): the exact Dirichlet-to-Neumann map of the monopole far field on the box. "dirichlet": the box grounded, which biases the resistance low by about \(\rho_n/(2\pi R)\) (for truncation studies).

    		 'robin'
    max_nodes int

    Resource limit of the axisymmetric model: the node count of the finer mesh, estimated before anything is assembled (the estimate errs high). Default 2 million: the solve needs about 4 GB per million nodes of the finer mesh, so about 8 GB at the limit.

    		 2000000
    max_nodes_3d int

    Resource limit of the three-dimensional model: the node count of its finer mesh, predicted before meshing and counted before the finer level is built. The solve adds about 2.9 GB per million nodes to the peak memory of the process (3.0 ... 3.1 GB with the process itself).

    		 2000000
    max_ports_3d int

    Resource limit of the three-dimensional model: the number of ports (every electrode and every leaking piece of a galvanic distributed conductor), checked before meshing. Default 100: every port costs one conjugate-gradient solve per mesh level, about 0.9 s per port and level at 600 000 nodes of the finer mesh.

    		 100
    model str

    "auto" (default): the axisymmetric model where it applies (rods on one axis, rings around it, no galvanic distributed conductor), the three-dimensional model otherwise; "axisymmetric" refuses every other world; "3d" forces the three-dimensional model.

    		 'auto'
    source_radius float | None

    3-D model: radius in m of the disc over which each wire's leakage is smoothed; None (default) takes 0.06 m (at least 2.2 bare wire radii, at most what the depth of the wires, their gap to the interfaces and the distance of wires that run beside each other — kept 1.5 source radii apart — allow).

    		 None
    growth float

    3-D model: growth of the element size per metre away from the wires (default 0.5; smaller is finer and slower).

    		 0.5
    concrete_resistivity float | None

    3-D model: None (default) applies every encased wire's own shell coefficient; a resistivity in Ω·m resolves the concrete as square prisms of conformal radius wire_radius around the encased (axis-aligned, straight) wires, shared where they meet (user decision Q40).

    		 None
    _concrete_mesh float | None

    Private, for the overlap study of user decision Q40 (see solid_earth()).

    		 None
    n_radial int | None

    Deprecated: the mesh controls of the equivalent-hemisphere mesh (0.15.0); a value has no effect and warns.

    		 None
    n_axial int | None

    Deprecated: the mesh controls of the equivalent-hemisphere mesh (0.15.0); a value has no effect and warns.

    		 None
    z_far_factor int | None

    Deprecated: the mesh controls of the equivalent-hemisphere mesh (0.15.0); a value has no effect and warns.

    		 None

    Returns:

    Type Description
    FieldResult

    Electrode potentials and currents (every electrode an equipotential port), point sources with the leakage distribution of the model, and metadata with fem_port_resistance (the extrapolated port resistance matrix in Ω, ports in world order, fem_ports), fem_port_resistance_levels (per mesh level), fem_error_estimate (largest relative difference of a diagonal entry between the extrapolated and the finer level; NaN with extrapolate=False), fem_error_estimate_transfer (3-D model: the same for the transfer entries; NaN for one port or one level), fem_model ("axisymmetric" or "3d": the model that ran), fem_mesh (size and time per level) and fem_r_far (box size in m).

    Raises:

    Type Description
    BackendCapabilityError

    With model="axisymmetric": if the world is not axisymmetric (an electrode other than a rod or a ring, a rod or ring off the common axis by more than 1e-3 of the smallest wire radius or gap, a galvanic distributed conductor), its electrodes touch, a ring wire reaches within 5 % of its radius to the soil surface, or a ring has no room for its mesh block (within about a wire radius, diagonally, of a rod's end edge); model="auto" solves these worlds with the three-dimensional model. 3-D model, before meshing: a wire too close to the soil surface or an interface for its smoothed source; wires that do not meet but run beside each other (side by side within 30° of parallel, a folded arm, a small ring around a rod head, two wires that meet at less than 10° or touch along their length) closer than 1.5 times the smallest source radius, and wires end to end in line with a gap, such as stacked rods, closer than 5 times it (the smallest source radius is 2.2 radii of the thickest bare wire of the world, so 3.3 and 11 such radii, axis to axis); wires that meet at 10° or more are left alone; resolved concrete around a wire that is not straight along x, y or z, or whose cover is so thin that the smoothed source does not reach beyond the metal. After meshing: conjugate gradients that do not converge (layer contrasts above about 300). The message names the backends that solve the world. A subclass of ValueError and NotImplementedError.
    ImportError

    If the world needs the three-dimensional model and the fem3d extra (scikit-fem, pyamg) is not installed.
    ValueError

    If an electrode or a galvanic distributed conductor lies at or above the soil surface (as every backend), or the world fails World.check.
    ResourceLimitError

    If the finer mesh would exceed max_nodes nodes (the 3-D model: max_nodes_3d, a prediction before meshing and the exact count before the finer level), or the 3-D model would solve more than max_ports_3d ports; where wires that run beside each other limited the source radius, the message says so.
    TypeError

    If world.soil is no soil model.

    Warns:

    Type Description
    MixedCoordinatesWarning

    For a world that mixes local and projected coordinates (user decision D5), as every backend.
    InterfaceContactWarning

    3-D model: for a rod end within one wire radius of a layer interface (audit W4R2A-03: a rod tip on 1000/30 Ohm m read +43 % against the solid rod, with an estimate of 6e-3) and for a horizontal wire within the reach of a contrasting one (audits W4A-07, W4B-02), where the smoothed line source shares the thin-wire error of the integral engines; once per rule and solve, as there. The axisymmetric model resolves rod end faces and ring wires and does not warn.
    DeprecationWarning

    For n_radial, n_axial or z_far_factor.
    Notes

    Without extrapolation the resistance of the axisymmetric model converges at second order and, in every case tested away from interfaces, from below; this is not guaranteed (the O-grid of a ring is not nested between levels), and next to an interface cut into a ring's mesh block it did not hold before that block was refined (audit W4A-01) and graded towards the points where the interface meets the wire (audit W4R2A-02: touching a 1000 times more conductive layer the levels converged at about first order, the default read -1.6e-2 with an estimate of 1.1e-2). The error estimate bounds the error of the extrapolated value while both levels lie on the same side of the converged value and the finer level's error is at most 1/2.5 of the coarser level's (about 1/3.9 is observed for rods and rings, 1/3.9 ... 1/4.0 for a ring touching a 100 or 1000 times more conductive layer).
